title: Novel α-Cyano indolylchalcone derivatives as potential candidates for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment (HepG2 cell line)
abstractText: Four novel α-cyano-indolylchalcone derivatives ( 3a, 3b, 5a, and 5b ), incorporating biologically active indole, pyrazole, and chalcone pharmacophores within a single molecular framework, were successfully synthesized and structurally characterized using FTIR, NMR ( 1 H and 1 3 C), and mass spectrometry. The cytotoxic potential of the synthesized compounds was evaluated against breast cancer (MCF7), hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2), and colorectal cancer (HCT116) cell lines using the MTT assay. Doxorubicin was used as a reference drug and exhibited an IC₅₀ value of 4.4 µg/mL against HepG2 cells. Among the synthesized derivatives, compounds 5a and 5b showed the highest cytotoxic activity, particularly against HepG2 cells, with IC₅₀ values of 49.01 and 21.89 µg/mL, respectively.To elucidate their mechanism of action, the apoptotic effects of compounds 5a and 5b were investigated using gene expression analysis, cell-cycle assessment, caspase activation assays, and flow cytometry. Treatment with both compounds resulted in significant upregulation of the pro-apoptotic genes Bax and p53 , downregulation of the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2 , activation of caspase-3 and caspase-9, and induction of G1-phase cell-cycle arrest. Flow cytometric analysis further confirmed enhanced apoptotic cell death in treated HepG2 cells.These findings demonstrate that α-cyano-indolylchalcone derivatives, particularly compound 5b, exert potent anticancer activity through activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway and inhibition of cell proliferation. The study highlights the therapeutic potential of integrating indole, pyrazole, and chalcone scaffolds into a single molecular architecture and identifies compounds 5a and 5b as promising lead candidates for the development of novel treatments for HepG2.

title: Peran Food Quality, Restaurant Atmosphere, dan Emotional Experience dalam Meningkatkan Customer Satisfaction pada Restoran IIBUMI di Kabupaten Padang Pariaman
abstractText: Customer satisfaction is an important indicator of restaurant performance and can be influenced by various aspects of the dining experience, including food quality, restaurant atmosphere, and emotional experience. This study aims to examine the effect of food quality, atmosphere, and emotional experience on customer satisfaction at IIBUMI Restaurant in Padang Pariaman Regency. This study employed a quantitative approach using a non-probability sampling technique. Data were collected from 110 respondents who had visited and experienced dining at IIBUMI Restaurant. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 25 through validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis for hypothesis testing. The results indicate that food quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Atmosphere also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Furthermore, emotional experience has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. These findings indicate that improving food quality, creating a conducive restaurant atmosphere, and providing positive emotional experiences are important aspects in enhancing customer satisfaction at IIBUMI Restaurant.

title: Mixed-Signal Front-End Design for Concurrent Acquisition of Electrophysiological and Hemodynamic Brain Signals
abstractText: Based on experimental evidence, multimodal neuro engineering applications in the case of electrophysiological monitoring and hemodynamic monitoring of a brain region demands simultaneous functionality, but is difficult because of the difference in signal amplitude, bandwidth and noise specifications that is very high indeed. Electrophysiological signals are microvolt-scale amplitude and bandwidth (KHz) signals, and hemodynamic signals are millivolt-scale amplitude and sub-10-Hz signals, so attempt to record both simultaneously is likely to be saturation artefact, crosstalk, and or timing error. The paper will discuss a mix signal front-end system that allows simultaneous capture of both modalities with a single and time synchronized signal chain. The proposed design uses dual analogue conditions along conditions along with modality selective gain and bandwidth isolation, and then an identical mixed-signal conversion stage, to synchronise sampling. To suppress inter-path interference and at the same time maintain sensitivity to low-amplitude electrophysiological signals a noise-optimised low-noise amplifier and frequency-selective filtering strategy is adopted. Noise in Analytical Noise Analytical noise models are developed to design circuits and choice parameters. Sub-microvolt input-referred noise Experimental validation of synthesised brain-signal emulation containable levels in combination with reliable concurrent acquisition of the electrophysiological path, low inter-modal crosstalk, and stable tracking of hemodynamic signals under simultaneous operation have been demonstrated. The findings affirm that, the proposed mixed-signal front-end offers scalable and low-energy efficient model of deployed multimodal brain-monitoring systems and facilitates compact and synchronised acquisitions architectures of next-generation neuro interface systems.

title: Jinoyat sodir etgan shaxslarni qayta ijtimoiylashtirishda probatsiya xizmatining o‘rni: amaliy faoliyat va uni takomillashtirish vazifalari
abstractText: This article examines the role of the probation service in the social reintegration of individuals who have committed criminal offenses, with particular attention to the relationship between supervision and practical support. The study aims to compare legal requirements with publicly reported practices and to identify priorities for improvement. Content and comparative analyses were conducted using two laws, two scholarly works, one international recommendation, and five official reports. The analysis identified individualized support, employment assistance, and staff training as key areas of probation activity. However, the official reports provided insufficient information to assess the long-term outcomes of the assistance provided. The article proposes a structured process comprising needs assessment, agreement on specific tasks, referral to relevant services, outcome monitoring, and program adjustment. Indicators related to service uptake and employment retention are also proposed for assessing implementation and outcomes. The practical effectiveness of the proposed measures requires further empirical evaluation.

title: Studi Naskah Kitab Tafsir Rawa`i’ alBayan Karya ‘Ali al-Sabuni
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji teks kitab Rawā’i‘ al-Bayān fī Tafsīr Āyāt al-Aḥkām min al-Qur’ān karya Muhammad ‘Ali al-Ṣābūnī. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian kualitatif dengan pendekatan kepustakaan (library research). Sumber data primer adalah kitab Rawā’i‘al-Bayān, sedangkan data sekunder diperoleh dari literatur yang relevan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa al-Ṣābūnī tidak hanya menafsirkan ayat-ayat hukum dengan pendekatan fikih melalui pemaparan pendapat para ulama, tetapi juga secara konsisten mengungkap hikmah al-tasyri‘pada bagian akhir penafsiran. Hikmah tersebut merupakan hasil dari analisis komprehensif terhadap aspek kebahasaan, asbāb al-nuzūl, munāsabah ayat, serta perbandingan pendapat ulama. Dengan demikian, tafsir ini menegaskan bahwa syariat Islam dibangun atas dasar kemaslahatan, keadilan, dan perlindungan terhadap nilai-nilai dasar kehidupan manusia. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan al-Ṣābūnī relevan dalam menjembatani pemahaman hukum Islam yang tidak hanya tekstual, tetapi juga kontekstual dan berorientasi pada tujuan syariat.

Islamic Educational Leadership Based on Islamic Epistemology in Responding to the Challenges of the Digital Age for Generation Alpha
abstractText: Digital transformation calls for Islamic educational leadership grounded in Islamic values to address the challenges faced by Generation Alpha, particularly regarding the validity of information, digital ethics, the protection of learners, and the cultivation of good manners. This study aims to develop a conceptual model of Islamic educational leadership based on Islamic epistemology. The research employs a qualitative approach through a literature review with a conceptual synthesis of the literature on Islamic epistemology, educational leadership, digital transformation, and the learning characteristics of Generation Alpha. Analysis was conducted through the identification of themes, the comparison of theoretical ideas, and the mapping of relationships between concepts. The results of the synthesis produced a model comprising four components: the epistemological foundation; principles of reasoning and decision-making; digital leadership actions; and educational outcome orientation. This model positions the integration of revelation, reason, and empirical experience as the foundation for decision-making, guided by the principles of tabayyun, amanah, justice, and the public good. The conceptual contribution of this research lies in its explanation of the relationship between Islamic epistemology, leaders’ decision-making mechanisms, and digital governance oriented towards learner development. The proposed model remains conceptual in nature and therefore requires empirical testing within Islamic educational institutions.

title: Analisis Dhabt dan Waqf QS. An-Nisa’ pada Manuskrip Al-Qur’an Kuno Milik Syaikh Abdurrahman Bintungan Tinggi
abstractText: Penelitian ini mengkaji sistem dhabt dan waqf pada mushaf Al-Qur’an kuno Surau Baru Bintungan Tinggi, khususnya pada Surah An-Nisa’, yang hingga kini belum pernah dianalisis secara mandiri dalam kajian manuskrip Nusantara. Mushaf ini menunjukkan sejumlah perbedaan mencolok dibandingkan mushaf Utsmani standar Indonesia, terutama pada aspek penandaan baca seperti tasydid, sukun, harakat, dan tanda mad, sehingga mengindikasikan adanya tradisi penyalinan lokal yang khas dan tidak melalui proses pentashhihan resmi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif–komparatif dengan data primer berupa mushaf tulisan tangan Syeikh Abdurrahman Bintungan Tinggi serta data sekunder dari berbagai literatur terkait. Analisis dilakukan melalui observasi fisik naskah, identifikasi unsur dhabt, pendokumentasian variasi penandaan baca, inventarisasi dan analisis tanda waqf, serta perbandingan sistematis dengan mushaf standar Indonesia. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mushaf ini tidak konsisten dalam penulisan tasydid, menampilkan penggunaan sukun yang berbeda, dan memperlihatkan variasi harakat termasuk adanya harakat ganda serta ketidakkonsistenan tanda mad pada sejumlah kategori seperti mad wajib muttashil, mad jaiz munfashil, maupun lafdzul jalalah. Pada aspek waqf, mushaf hanya menampilkan tanda berhenti pada akhir ayat berupa lingkaran merah tanpa nomor ayat dan tidak memuat waqf pertengahan ayat, bahkan beberapa akhir ayat tidak diberi tanda atau ditandai secara berbeda dari mushaf standar. Temuan-temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa mushaf tersebut merepresentasikan model penulisan tradisional yang sederhana, personal, dan sangat dipengaruhi oleh gaya penyalin serta tradisi lokal Surau Baru Bintungan Tinggi. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi penting bagi studi filologi dan kajian mushaf Nusantara dengan menghadirkan data baru dari tradisi penyalinan Minangkabau, meskipun penelitian ini memiliki keterbatasan karena hanya mengkaji satu surah dan naskah berada dalam kondisi fisik yang rusak sehingga tidak seluruh bagian mushaf dapat dianalisis secara menyeluruh.

title: Arabert with Graph Attention for Imbalanced Arabic Sentiment Classification: An Ablation Study of Fusion Strategies
abstractText: Purpose: This study examines whether combining AraBERT with a Graph Attention Network (GAT) over a semantic text graph improves three-class classification. Design/Methodology/Approach: Experiments were conducted on hotel reviews (HARD, 392,512 texts) and book reviews (LABR, 59,620 texts). Both corpora are imbalanced in almost identical proportions — negative 13.06%, neutral 19.92%, positive 67.01% in HARD, and 13.13%, 19.47%, 67.40% in LABR. A stratified 70/15/15 split preserves these proportions, giving evaluation partitions of 58,878 and 8,944 reviews, respectively. We compared four configurations: AraBERT alone (M1), a frozen encoder feeding the graph network (M2), a fine-tuned encoder whose sentence representation is replaced by the pooled graph states (M3), and a fine-tuned encoder whose pooled graph states are fused with the retained CLS representation (M4). Each configuration was trained with three seeds on a fixed stratified split. Research Limitation: The paired t-test over three seeds does not reach significance in either corpus. Findings: On LABR, M4 obtained the highest F1-Macro (0.6263 ± 0.0036 against 0.6226 ± 0.0036 for M1), and McNemar's test was significant in two of the three seeds. On HARD, the ordering was reversed (0.8337 ± 0.0040 for M1 against 0.8304 ± 0.0028 for M4). M3 did not exceed the baseline, and M2 fell clearly below it. Practical Implication: Establishing a clearer benefit will require a more precise graph, in particular one derived from syntactic parsing rather than lexical matching, and a tighter form of integration than the concatenation used here. Social Implication: Sentiment analysis is a natural language processing technique which seeks to determine whether the expressed sentiment is positive, negative or neutral so that an institution/researcher can gain insights from a large set of unstructured data. Originality/Value: The study isolates the manner of combination rather than the presence of the graph: fusing the pooled graph states with the retained CLS representation improves on the baseline, whereas substituting them for it does not, a distinction not previously separated for Arabic document-level sentiment.

title: Potentiation of the Immunostimulant Effect of Tetramisole: Revisiting Approach
abstractText: The effect of Tetramisole Tet and its combination with incomplete Freund adjuvant IFA in egg albumin EA specific immune primed rabbit groups were investigated. The immune test battery were including; innate immune cell phagocytosis, B cell antibody formation and lymphoid cell blasto-genesis. The phagocytic activity of the EA immune primed rabbits was evaluated by nitro-blue tetrazolium reduction test, B cell antibody synthesis were evaluated on the rabbits immune sera by passive heam-agglutination assay and cellular immunity was determined by the activity of lymphoid cell to the mitogen ConA in lymphoid cell culture. Tet and IFA when inoculated separately, induce an increase in phagocytic activity, but with non-significant potentiating effect. Though, the incorporation of Tet and IFA induces significant potentiation. The anti-EA antibody synthesis and lymphoblast transformation were enhanced by Tetramisole and such enhancement was high potentiated by IFA incorporation. Thus, Tetramisole in this test animal model enhanced phagocytic activity, antiEA antibody synthesis as well as cellular immunity, these effects were much more potentiated by IFA incorporation. Safe oily fraction like short chain fatty acids can be of promising immune-modulating potential on incorporation with Tetramizole for therapy of human chronic infectious and immune mediated diseases

title: Prediksi Pengiriman Bermasalah PT Lion Express Palembang: Perbandingan Tiga Model Klasifikasi
abstractText: Pengiriman bermasalah (delivery exception) menambah biaya penanganan dan menurunkan kepuasan pelanggan, tetapi proporsinya yang kecil menyulitkan identifikasi manual. Penelitian ini membandingkan Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, dan Random Forest untuk memprediksi pengiriman yang belum berstatus bukti pengiriman (non-POD) pada PT Lion Express Cabang Palembang berdasarkan area tujuan, berat tertagih, siklus, dan hari pengiriman, serta mengevaluasi penanganan ketidakseimbangan kelas. Data terdiri atas 32.475 transaksi Agustus 2026 dengan proporsi kelas bermasalah 8,52%. Data dibagi per nomor resi untuk mencegah kebocoran, hyperparameter dioptimasi dengan validasi silang 5-lipatan berkriteria PR-AUC, dan ketidakseimbangan kelas ditangani dengan SMOTENC. Pada data uji, Random Forest memperoleh ROC-AUC 0,745 (CI 95%: 0,719–0,770) dan PR-AUC 0,370 (4,3 kali nilai acak 0,085); selisihnya dengan Decision Tree tidak signifikan. SMOTENC tidak meningkatkan ROC-AUC maupun PR-AUC, tetapi menggeser titik operasi, sedangkan tuning menaikkan PR-AUC sekitar 0,03. Area tujuan merupakan fitur terpenting, diikuti hari, siklus, dan berat tertagih. Pada validasi temporal, ROC-AUC turun menjadi 0,666 dan PR-AUC 0,143, sehingga model lebih sesuai untuk prioritisasi pengawasan daripada keputusan otomatis.

Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
abstractText: Abstract Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

title: Analisis Kepuasan ASN terhadap Mock Detector Menggunakan TAM dan K-Means
abstractText: The implementation of Global Positioning System (GPS)-based attendance systems for Civil Servants (ASN) facilitates real-time location verification, but it also introduces the risk of location manipulation through fake GPS applications. This study analyzes ASN acceptance and satisfaction with the Mock Detector application as a supporting mechanism for attendance security using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the K-Means algorithm. A quantitative survey was conducted using questionnaires distributed to 53 ASN users of a GPS-based attendance system. The research variables were Perceived Usefulness (PU), Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU), and User Satisfaction (US). TAM analysis was performed through instrument testing and multiple linear regression, while K-Means was applied to segment respondent characteristics. The results show that PU and PEOU have positive and significant effects on US. The regression model is US=0.132+0.645(PU)+0.393(PEOU), with an R Square of 0.712. Clustering produced three groups: Cluster 0 with 22 respondents, Cluster 1 with 23 respondents, and Cluster 2 with 8 respondents, representing low, moderate, and high acceptance levels, respectively. These findings indicate that perceived usefulness and ease of use are important factors in Mock Detector acceptance, while K-Means segmentation provides user-group characteristics that can support evaluation and improvement of the attendance system.

title: When to Use t Test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA: A Step-by-Step Guide for Novice Educational Researchers
abstractText: Selecting an appropriate statistical test remains a challenge for novice educational researchers, particularly when distinguishing among parametric procedures with different requirements and analytical purposes. This paper provides a practical guide for selecting the t-test, ANOVA, ANCOVA, MANOVA, and MANCOVA in quantitative educational research. The guide begins with hypothesis testing and variable classification, followed by normality assessment and consideration of data transformation before selecting the appropriate statistical procedure. Each test is explained according to its purpose, assumptions, research question, types, decision criteria, and interpretation. The paper emphasizes the necessity of choosing statistical tests based on the research hypothesis structure, number of groups, dependent variables, and covariates, rather than by familiarity with statistical software. The guide is designed to assist novice education researchers to make sound statistical choices and improve the validity and interpretability of their quantitative research results.

title: Learning epithelial elasticity via local tension remodeling
abstractText: Abstract Biological materials such as epithelial tissues continuously remodel their internal structure in response to mechanical forces, but whether this adaptation amounts to a genuine form of physical learning has remained unclear. Here we show that an active vertex model of epithelial sheets, equipped with a single local, mechanosensitive tensionremodeling rule, exhibits the three canonical hallmarks of learning matter. First, at the scale of a single junction, repeated contractile pulses produce habituation: a diminishing, history-dependent response that encodes a memory of prior stimulation. Second, at the tissue scale, a localized stimulus writes a long-range mechanical memory that biases the response to a later, distant stimulus. We derive a continuum theory showing that this memory is transmitted as a system-wide elastic bias and predict its dependence on tissue size and remodeling rate. Third, under cyclic bulk driving, the tissue can be trained to a target mechanical state, autonomously tuning its Poisson ratio to auxetic (negative) values through directed remodeling rather than designed geometry. We further derive an effective viscoelastic memory kernel that distinguishes this adaptive tissue from a passive vertex model. Together, these results identify a candidate mechanism for physical learning in epithelia, in which the ratio of contraction to extension remodeling rates acts as the central control parameter for programmable, history-dependent tissue-scale rheology.

Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation strategies for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
abstractText: Abstract Background Refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is almost invariably fatal. Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a feasible rescue treatment and may improve outcomes in highly selected patients. On-scene and hospital-based ECPR each have distinct strengths and limitations, but a real-world comparison of their association with survival is lacking. Methods We analysed a multicentric prospective registry of 52,505 OHCAs in the Greater Paris area (France), from May 2011 to August 2024. We quantified the association between an on-scene ECPR strategy and survival to hospital discharge with favourable neurological outcome (defined as a Cerebral Performance Category 1 or 2), compared to a hospital-based ECPR strategy, adjusting for established prognostic factors, with multivariable and propensity score methods. Results A total of 1,031 patients treated with ECPR were included (16% were female, median age 50 years). Of them, 256 patients received on-scene ECPR, with favourable neurological outcome in 13%, compared to 6% in 775 patients with hospital-based ECPR ( P < 0.01). The time from CPR to ECPR initiation was shorter with the on-scene strategy (70 min [60–84] vs. 93 min [75–113], P < 0.01). In multivariable analysis, the on-scene ECPR strategy was independently associated with favourable neurological outcome (OR, 2.3; 95% CI, 1.4–3.9; P < 0.01). These findings were consistent in propensity score–matched analyses (OR, 2.1; 95% CI, 1.1–4.1; P = 0.03). For IPTW, OR 2.3, 95%CI 1.4–3.9, P<0.01). At one year of follow-up, there was a significant association between the on-scene ECPR strategy and overall survival, (log-rank test, P < 0.01). Conclusions In this large, population-based registry of refractory OHCA, the on-scene ECPR strategy was associated with a significantly shorter time to ECPR initiation and favourable neurological outcome at hospital discharge when compared with the hospital-based ECPR strategy. These findings highlight the potential interest of an on-scene ECPR strategy in selected patients, but further investigations are warranted. Large, randomized controlled trials and studies conducted in diverse healthcare systems are needed to clarify its role more precisely, particularly regarding long-term neurological recovery, cost-effectiveness, and broader system-level impact.

Exploring the Relationship between AI Competency and Professional Identity in Language Education: A Mixed-methods Study
abstractText: The integration of artifi cial intelligence (AI) in education is increasingly prevalent; however, the implications of AI competency forprofessional identity remain underexplored. Building on Sociocultural Theory and Possible Selves Theory, this convergent mixed-methods study examines the relationship between AI competency and instructor characteristics with professional identity among 111Turkish EFL instructors. Validated scales measuring AI competency and professional identity were administered alongside semi-structured interviews with 12 participants. Quantitative analyses revealed that AI competency signifi cantly predicts professionalidentity (β = .295, p = .002). Prior AI exposure markedly diff erentiated competency levels, while age and teaching experience had nosignifi cant eff ect. Qualitative fi ndings identifi ed three identity trajectories (strengthening, neutrality, and questioning) shaped by beliefs,emotions, institutional support, and instructional experience. We propose a novel interpretive mapping of these trajectories onto thehoped-for, expected, and feared dimensions of professional self-representation, off ering a theoretically parsimonious lens forunderstanding why instructors with equivalent AI competency levels exhibit divergent identity responses. The study highlights theimportance of professional development that goes beyond technical training to include guided, refl ective, and emotionally resonantexploration connecting AI skills with pedagogical values and ethical awareness.

title: PENINGKATAN HASIL BELAJAR MATEMATIKA KELAS V SD MELALUI PROJECT-BASED LEARNING BERBASIS SURVEI PADA PENYAJIAN DATA
abstractText: Murid sekolah dasar masih mengalami kesulitan memahami dan menyajikan data dalam bentuk piktogram dan diagram batang, sementara pembelajaran yang berpusat pada guru kurang memberikan pengalaman yang kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan hasil belajar matematika murid kelas V pada materi penyajian data melalui penerapan Project-Based Learning (PjBL) berbasis survei. Penelitian menggunakan Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) model Kemmis dan McTaggart dalam dua siklus, masing-masing meliputi perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi, dengan subjek 32 murid kelas V SD Negeri 1 Tukmudal. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, penilaian proyek, presentasi, dan tes tertulis. Kemudian data hasil belajar dianalisis secara deskriptif kuantitatif melalui perhitungan rata-rata dan persentase ketuntasan, sedangkan data observasi dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata hasil belajar meningkat dari 67,1 pada Siklus I menjadi 79,4 pada Siklus II, dan persentase murid dengan nilai minimal 75 naik dari 25% menjadi 59%. Dapat disimpulkan bahwa PjBL berbasis survei sederhana dapat meningkatkan hasil belajar sekaligus mendorong keterlibatan aktif murid dalam memahami penyajian data. Guru disarankan merancang proyek survei dengan alokasi waktu yang memadai pada setiap tahap, dan penelitian lanjutan disarankan menguji ketahanan peningkatan tersebut dalam jangka waktu yang lebih panjang.

title: Acidosis as a metabolic barrier to immunotherapy: mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities
abstractText: Abstract Immune evasion remains a major obstacle to cancer immunotherapy and arises from multifaceted mechanisms. Among these, the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME) constitutes a critical physicochemical barrier that orchestrates immunosuppression. In this narrative review, we summarize the principal mechanisms through which TME acidosis remodels the immune landscape. Acidosis impairs the immunosurveillance and cytotoxic functions of innate and adaptive effector cells while promoting the expansion and suppressive potency of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs). Preclinical studies indicate that targeting tumor acidosis can partially restore antitumor immune function and may mitigate resistance to immunotherapy. These findings support biological plausibility, but they derive primarily from in vitro systems and murine models, corroborated by in silico analyses. Clinical evidence, however, remains limited to early-phase safety and target-engagement studies, and translation to patients is therefore not yet established. We further consider pH imaging as an emerging translational tool for patient selection and pharmacodynamic monitoring of pH-directed interventions. Targeting metabolic acidity is a biologically plausible and preclinically supported strategy that warrants rigorous clinical evaluation, ideally guided by non-invasive assessment of tumor pH. Para Além da Técnica: Competências da Formação Docente na Construção de uma Educação Inclusiva e Equitativa
abstractText: This theoretical essay investigates the competencies required in the initial and continuing training of teachers for the consolidation of an inclusive and equitable teaching practice. It starts from the premise that, despite the advanced Brazilian legal framework, a gap persists between regulations and classroom reality, whose overcoming is intrinsically linked to the adequate preparation of educators. The analysis further incorporates the most recent normative trajectory of Brazilian special education, from the National Inclusive Special Education Policy (Decree No. 12,686/2025) to its regulation through MEC Ordinance No. 421/2026, evidencing that the improvement of the legal framework does not, by itself, dispense with adequate teacher training. The study, of a bibliographic nature, problematizes the gaps in traditional training models and advocates for a transition to a reflective training paradigm. The analysis focuses on mapping and discussing a fundamental triad of competencies: socioemotional (empathy, resilience, collaboration), pedagogical (curriculum flexibility, procedural assessment, peer work), and technological (mastery of assistive and digital technologies). It is concluded that the effectiveness of inclusion requires a curricular restructuring in teacher training, transversally integrating these competencies through meaningful supervised internships and contextualized continuing education, to equip teachers to respond creatively and critically to student diversity, transforming the inclusive ideal into everyday pedagogical practice.

Prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles within paediatric ovarian tissue: recommendations for systematic subclassification
abstractText: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Do premenarcheal girls have a high proportion of morphologically abnormal ovarian follicles? SUMMARY ANSWER A higher prevalence of follicles with an abnormal number of oocytes and nuclei was found in premenarcheal ovarian tissue compared with postmenarcheal tissue. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Morphological aberrations of ovarian follicles, including multi-nuclear oocytes and multi-ovular follicles, have been documented across species, including humans. These specific morphological aberrations, together with other types of abnormal follicles, are more prevalent in the ovaries of children and decline in number with age. However, detailed studies of the prevalence of multi-nuclear and multi-ovular follicles in paediatric ovarian tissue are limited. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION This was an observational study of the ovaries of children and adolescents who underwent ovarian cryopreservation prior to chemotherapy. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS The study recruited participants aged 0–18 years who underwent ovarian tissue cryopreservation at a single centre. Haematoxylin and eosin-stained slides of ovarian biopsies were scanned and analysed to determine follicle number and aberrations in morphology and the cortical area was measured. Abnormal follicles were defined as those with an abnormal number of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Relationships with menarcheal status (premenarcheal; postmenarcheal) and age were assessed. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE A total of 149 participants’ ovarian samples were evaluated in the study, of whom 67 (45%) had follicles with abnormal numbers of oocytes or oocyte nuclei. Amongst 117 participants who had adequate follicle numbers, these abnormal follicle types accounted for 3.8% (902/23 891) of the total number of follicles and were significantly more common in premenarcheal girls (52/80; 65.0%) compared with postmenarcheal girls (15/37; 40.5%; P = 0.013). Ovular abnormalities (in 76.7% of abnormal follicles) were more common than nuclear abnormalities (in 23.3% of abnormal follicles; P < 0.001). Bi-ovular primordial follicles were the most common abnormality, comprising 54% of the total abnormal follicle population and were present in 41.9% of participants. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION Small ovarian biopsies were analysed, which may not fully represent the whole ovary. There is also a limited number of participants in each menarcheal group. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS Our study highlights that although follicle numbers are high in the prepubertal ovary, there was also a high proportion of follicles containing abnormal numbers of oocytes and oocyte nuclei. Further longitudinal and functional studies are recommended to determine whether this impacts fertility and the longevity of function following ovarian tissue grafting for restoration of fertility in these participants. Our work supports a separate multioocytic follicle class within the NICHD follicle classification, and we suggest expanding it to include a distinct multinuclear follicle category (oocyte contains more than one nucleus), as these likely represent different aberrations in oogenesis or folliculogenesis. This classification with clear definitions and nomenclature may improve consistency in reporting and facilitate future research. title: Impact of sonochemistry on synthesis and physicochemical properties of heterogeneous catalysts for gaseous environmental abatement
abstractText: Abstract The phenomenon of acoustic cavitation (the formation, oscillation, growth, and implosive collapse of tiny bubbles filled with dissolved gases and liquid vapor) generated by the irradiation of a liquid medium with ultrasound has established itself as an important tool in various branches of chemistry. The use of ultrasonic irradiation in chemical processes is known as “sonochemistry.” Among the applications of sonochemistry, the involvement of ultrasound in materials synthesis can provide a fast, straightforward method for preparing heterogeneous catalysts compared to conventional methods, thanks to the chemical and physical effects of acoustic cavitation (excited species, shockwaves, microjets, sonoluminescence). The catalytic processes involved in the transformation of greenhouse gases are attracting greater attention for their role in addressing the major environmental problem of global warming. The application of ultrasonic irradiation results in catalysts with enhanced structural, textural, and morphological properties, including specific surface area, particle size distribution, and dispersion of the active phase on the support. Hence, ultrasonic-assisted synthesis of catalysts yields materials with better activity and stability than those obtained by classical preparation methods, which is particularly important for the development of heterogeneous catalysis.

title: Endometrial compaction and ongoing pregnancy in modified natural cycle frozen euploid embryo transfer: a prospective multicentre cohort study with standardized transvaginal ultrasound assessment
abstractText: Abstract STUDY QUESTION Does endometrial compaction, assessed by transvaginal ultrasound at two measurement time points, predict ongoing pregnancy in patients undergoing single euploid blastocyst transfer in a modified natural cycle frozen embryo transfer (mNC-FET)? SUMMARY ANSWER Endometrial compaction of ≥5% between the day of ovulation triggering and the day of embryo transfer was not associated with ongoing pregnancy rate or any secondary reproductive outcome in this prospective multicentre cohort. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Endometrial compaction—a reduction in endometrial thickness (EMT) following progesterone-induced secretory transformation—has been proposed as a potential marker of endometrial receptivity in FET cycles. However, existing evidence is conflicting. Retrospective studies have reported positive associations between compaction and ongoing pregnancy in programmed cycles, while prospective data, including the only prior study restricted to euploid single FET, have not confirmed this relationship. Crucially, most studies have used transabdominal ultrasound for the transfer-day measurement, a recognized source of measurement error. No prospective study has examined compaction exclusively in mNC-FET using transvaginal ultrasound at both time points. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION Prospective multicentre observational cohort study conducted between March 2023 and March 2025 across six assisted reproduction units of Instituto Bernabeu group (Spain). A total of 207 patients who met all inclusion criteria and completed the full protocol were analysed. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS Women aged 18–50 years undergoing mNC-FET with a single euploid blastocyst (confirmed by preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy via next-generation sequencing) were included. EMT was measured transvaginally at T1 (day of hCG trigger) and T2 (day of embryo transfer). Compaction was defined as a ≥5% reduction in EMT from T1 to T2. Additional thresholds of ≥10% and ≥15% were evaluated as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was ongoing pregnancy, defined as foetal cardiac activity at 10 weeks of gestation. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusting for age, previous live births, previous miscarriages, BMI, and oocyte origin. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE Of 207 patients, 58 (28.0%) met the compaction criterion (≥5%). The compaction group had a significantly greater T1 EMT (9.55 ± 1.54 mm vs 8.39 ± 1.14 mm, P < 0.001) and a lower T2 EMT (7.91 ± 1.19 mm vs 9.75 ± 1.55 mm, P < 0.001). Ongoing pregnancy rates were 50.0% in the compaction group versus 53.7% in the non-compaction group (P = 0.633). This difference was not significant on multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio 0.80, 95% CI 0.38–1.67, P = 0.546). The null association was consistent across all compaction thresholds (≥10%: P = 0.674; ≥15%: P = 0.928) and across all secondary outcomes, including clinical pregnancy rate (56.9% vs 59.1%, P = 0.777), biochemical pregnancy loss (10.8% vs 8.3%, P = 0.737), and early pregnancy loss rate (12.1% vs 9.1%, P = 0.734). The overall ongoing pregnancy rate was 52.7% (109/207). LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION The distribution between groups was asymmetric (28% compaction vs 72% non-compaction), deviating from the balanced allocation anticipated at protocol design, which may reduce statistical power. Although both measurements were transvaginal, a subset of T1 measurements from international patients were performed at external centres and validated remotely by Instituto Bernabeu’s physicians. Live birth data were only partially available at the time of analysis; however, ongoing pregnancy at 10 weeks is a validated and widely accepted surrogate for live birth in reproductive medicine trials. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS These findings do not support the hypothesis that endometrial compaction is associated with improved reproductive outcomes in mNC-FET with euploid embryos. The consistent null result across multiple thresholds and outcomes, obtained with a fully standardized transvaginal ultrasound methodology, strengthens the current evidence base. Routine assessment of endometrial compaction with the aim of identifying patients with a favourable prognosis does not appear to be clinically justified in this setting; indeed, acting upon compaction status could lead to unnecessary cycle cancellations in patients who would otherwise achieve ongoing pregnancy. The funding body had no role in the study design, data collection, analysis or interpretation of the data, preparation of the manuscript, or decision to submit the manuscript for publication. No personal payments, financial incentives, or commercial benefits were received by any author in relation to this work. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER NCT05960370.

abstractText: Artikel ini mengkaji sejauh mana model Think Aloud Pair Problem Solving (TAPPS) berkaitan dengan tingkat kesadaran metakognitif siswa ketika mengerjakan soal matematika berbasis Higher Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) pada topik peluang. Desain yang dipilih adalah quasi experiment berpola Posttest-Only Control Group, dengan satu rombongan belajar berperan sebagai kelompok perlakuan dan satu lagi sebagai pembanding. Kelompok perlakuan berjumlah 37 siswa dan diajar dengan TAPPS, sementara kelompok pembanding berjumlah 35 siswa dan menerima pengajaran direct earning; penentuan kedua kelompok memakai teknik purposive sampling atas dasar kesetaraan kemampuan awal. Kesadaran metakognitif diukur melalui soal HOTS yang menyasar tiga aspek, yaitu merencanakan, memantau, dan mengevaluasi. Pengujian statistik mencakup normalitas (Shapiro-Wilk), homogenitas varians (Lavene’s Test), dan uji beda Mann-Whitney U untuk data yang tidak berdistribusi normal. Hasilnya, terdapat selisih yang bermakna secara statistik antara kedua kelompok (Asymp. Sig. = 0,003; α = 0,05). Skor rata-rata kelompok TAPPS mencapai 66,00, unggul atas kelompok pembanding yang berada di angka 59,83. Ditinjau dari kategorinya, mayoritas siswa kelompok TAPPS berhasil masuk kategori Strategic Use dan sebagian kecil menjangkau Reflective Use, sedangkan kelompok pembanding didominasi kategori Aware Use. Dengan kata lain, penerapan TAPPS tampak berasosiasi dengan taraf metakognisi yang lebih tinggi dalam menuntaskan soal HOTS, meskipun simpulan ini perlu dibaca dengan mempertimbangkan keterbatasan rancangan satu kelas per kelompok.

abstractText: This paper conducts a thematic content analysis of evaluations of a lesson on Scientific Theory within the microteaching context, guided by Ludwik Fleck's epistemology. The objective was to identify perceptions and construct analytical categories that reveal the epistemological and didactic challenges in transposing scientific knowledge into the school environment. The analysis demonstrated significant tensions, particularly in distinguishing between myth and scientific theory and in the construction of hypotheses, revealing the influence of thought styles on teaching practice. The collaborative reflection between the supervisor and the trainee teacher proved essential for interpreting these tensions, moving beyond a merely technical view of teaching. When critically analyzed, microteaching emerges as a powerful tool for developing the future teacher's understanding of science as a social and collective entity.

title: Right Iliac Fossa Mass: A Diagnostic Dilemma
abstractText: Introduction: A right iliac fossa mass presents a frequent surgical challenge. In tuberculosis endemic regions, hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis can closely mimic cecal carcinoma clinically, radiologically and colonoscopically. Case Presentation: A 40-year-old male presented with a palpable RIF lump, intermittent abdominal pain, anorexia and weight loss. Laboratory investigations revealed anemia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography scan demonstrated asymmetric circumferential mural thickening (21 mm) of the cecum and ascending colon with luminal narrowing, intramural calcifications and pericolic lymphadenopathy, suspicious for malignancy. Colonoscopy revealed a friable, non-negotiable ulceroproliferative mass. Colonoscopic biopsy demonstrated granulomatous colitis with epithelioid cells and multinucleated giant cells without evidence of malignancy. Due to severe luminal stenosis and persistent suspicion of malignancy, right hemicolectomy was performed. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen revealed caseating epithelioid granulomas, Langhans giant cells and tuberculous lymphadenitis, with no dysplasia or malignancy, establishing a diagnosis of hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis. The patient was subsequently initiated on antitubercular therapy. Conclusion: Hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis can simulate cecal carcinoma at every diagnostic step. While uncomplicated intestinal tuberculosis responds effectively to medical therapy, surgical resection remains crucial when complications arise or when malignancy cannot be confidently excluded preoperatively. High clinical suspicion and thorough histopathological evaluation are critical to guide definitive management.

title: Comparative Evaluation of TOON and JSON Serialization Formats for Token Efficiency, Answer Accuracy, and Structural Reliability in DeepSeek
abstractText: The increasing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) requires efficient structured-data serialization to reduce token consumption and operational costs without compromising accuracy. Token-Oriented Object Notation (TOON) offers an alternative to JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), but its performance on DeepSeek remains insufficiently evaluated. Objective: This study evaluates token efficiency, answer accuracy, structural validation reliability, and estimated API processing costs across six serialization formats. Methods: A descriptive comparative experiment employed 11 official benchmark datasets, five synthetic datasets, and 209 evaluation questions. A total of 1,154 DeepSeek API requests were performed, while offline token consumption was measured separately using the o200k_base tokenizer. Results: TOON reduced token consumption by 58.8% for flat datasets and 21.9% for mixed-structure datasets compared with pretty-printed JSON. TOON achieved the highest observed answer accuracy (96.2%), compared with JSON (95.2%), although structural validation accuracy remained at 60.0%. Implications: The findings support workload-dependent serialization selection and emphasize the importance of deterministic schema validation and output-token monitoring for reliable, cost-efficient LLM applications. Originality: This study extends the official TOON benchmarking framework to DeepSeek and integrates token efficiency, accuracy, structural reliability, and cost evaluation, demonstrating that compression advantages do not necessarily correspond to improved accuracy or lower processing costs.

title: Eco-friendly adsorptive stripping square wave voltammetric quantification of lumefantrine using manganese dioxide-based screen-printed sensors
abstractText: As one of the deadliest vector-borne diseases worldwide, malaria represents one of the most severe global public health problems. Therefore, monitoring antimalarial drugs is necessary to face enormous challenges with substandard and falsified antimalarial drugs. The construction and full characterization of carbonaceous screen-printed sensors integrated with manganese oxide nanoparticles (Mn 2 O 3 NPs/SPCEs) were presented for sensitive and selective adsorptive stripping square wave voltammetric (AdSSWV) determination of the Anti-Malarial Drug: Lumefantrine (LUM) in artemether–lumefantrine (AL) fixed-dose combination (FDC). The enrichment of the electrode surface with Mn 2 O 3 NPs enhanced the electrochemical oxidation of LUM at 0.74 V in Britton-Robinson buffer (BR at pH 6). Comprehensive computational density functional theory (DFT) studies combined with electroanalytical investigations revealed an adsorption-controlled mechanism accompanied by the transfer of two protons/electrons localized on the nitrogen atom (N5). Mn 2 O 3 NPs/SPCEs showed a linear response (r 2 =0.9981) covering the LUM concentration from 0.030 to 2.608 µg mL⁻ 1 and an LOD value of 10 ngmL -1 . The proposed disposable sensors exhibited reproducible performance within an extended storage period up to 3 months. Based on the therapeutic impact of LUM, the Mn 2 O 3 NPs/SPCEs voltammetric sensors were effectively tested for monitoring the dissolution and quantification of LUM in marketed formulations and biological fluids with acceptable recoveries compared with the official analytical protocol. The green analytical metrics were evaluated, highlighting the environmental friendliness of the Mn 2 O 3 NPs-based sensors.

title: Hyperinflammatory septic shock during immune reconstitution: Temporal association with HA-330 hemoadsorption: A case report
abstractText: Introduction: Immune-recovery phases after intensive chemotherapy can abruptly trigger hyperinflammatory responses that amplify vasoplegia in septic shock. Recognizing this phenotype is crucial, particularly when the inflammatory burden is disproportionate to the source of infection. Case presentation: A 56-year-old woman with acute B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia developed sudden vasoplegic shock during profound neutropenia with Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) support following administration of hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, adriamycin (doxorubicin), and dexamethasone ( Hyper-CVAD). She presented with severe hyperlactatemia (11 mmol/L), C-reactive protein (CRP) 232 mg/L, procalcitonin >100 ng/mL, and extreme elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) (371,464 pg/mL). Despite timely broad-spectrum antibiotics, hydrocortisone, aggressive fluid resuscitation, and high-dose dual vasopressors, profound vasoplegia persisted. Urine output remained partially preserved (0.33–0.93 mL/kg/h) in the setting of predominantly vasodilatory circulatory failure. Intervention and outcome: Three sessions of HA-330 hemoadsorption (Jafron Biomedical, Zhuhai, China) over 72 hours were initiated after failure of conventional therapy. IL-6 declined from 371,464 to 23,629 pg/mL after the first session and to 517 pg/mL after the third session. This was temporally associated with progressive reduction in vasopressor requirements and lactate normalization. Hemodynamic stability was achieved with improved organ perfusion. Conclusions: This case highlights a cytokine-dominant vasoplegic septic shock phenotype during immune recovery, marked by extraordinary IL-6 elevation despite partially preserved renal perfusion. The temporal alignment between hemoadsorption, cytokine reduction, and hemodynamic improvement is hypothesis-generating and underscores the potential role of inflammatory burden in certain hyperinflammatory shock states.

title: Dynamics of Verbal Bullying and School Ecosystem Responses in Junior High Education: An Analysis of Excessive Joking Culture and Character-Based Interventions
abstractText: Verbal bullying at the junior high school level is frequently normalized as ordinary social interaction, despite its significant detrimental impact on students' emotional well-being and academic development. This descriptive qualitative case study aimed to examine the manifestations of verbal bullying, analyze its socio-cultural determinants and psychological impacts on students, and evaluate the effectiveness of institutional responses within the school ecosystem. The study involved 50 participants, including students, subject teachers, Guidance and Counseling (BK) teachers, and administrative staff at SMP Kartiyoso Semarang. Data were gathered through social interaction observations, open-ended questionnaires, and in-depth interviews, followed by interactive data analysis validated through triangulation techniques. The findings revealed that verbal bullying at SMP Kartiyoso Semarang predominantly manifested through negative labeling (name-calling), physical mocking, abusive language, and degrading jokes disguised as friendly banter (excessive teasing). Primary catalysts included peer group pressure, low emotional literacy, and expansion into digital spaces (cyber-verbal bullying). Psychologically, victims suffered from diminished self-efficacy, social anxiety, embarrassment, and reduced learning motivation. The study concludes that current reactive institutional interventions remain insufficient in preventing recurrent incidents. Consequently, strengthening the institutional role of SMP Kartiyoso Semarang requires integrating emotional literacy into the curriculum, strengthening interactive teacher supervision, establishing confidential reporting channels, and fostering sustainable synergy with parents.

The Effect Of Service Quality On Consumer Loyalty With Consumer Satisfaction As An Intervening Variable At Sibmont Tire Repair Shop In Aceh Besar
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality on consumer loyalty at SibMont Ban Workshop in Aceh Besar, with consumer satisfaction as an intervening variable. This study employed a quantitative approach with an associative research design. Data were collected through questionnaires using a Likert scale. The data analysis techniques included validity testing, reliability testing, classical assumption tests, linear regression analysis, t-test, coefficient of determination (R²), path analysis, and Sobel test using SPSS version 27. The results showed that service quality has a positive and significant effect on consumer loyalty. Service quality also has a positive and significant effect on consumer satisfaction. Furthermore, consumer satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on consumer loyalty. The mediation test results indicated that consumer satisfaction mediates the effect of service quality on consumer loyalty. Thus, consumer satisfaction acts as an intervening variable in the relationship between service quality and consumer loyalty, with partial mediation. These findings indicate that improving the service quality provided by SibMont Ban Workshop in Aceh Besar can increase consumer satisfaction and ultimately strengthen consumer loyalty.

title: Communicating Mental Health Inequalities: Experiences of Children in Child-Headed Households in Peri-Urban Epworth, Zimbabwe
abstractText: This study examined how mental health inequalities are communicated and socially negotiated by children in child-headed households (CHHs) in the Epworth settlement. Positioned within the sociology of communication, the study treats disclosure and silence as its central objects of analysis. Three objectives guided the study: to explore how CHH children communicate and make sense of their mental health challenges, to examine the structural barriers limiting their access to mental health services, and to identify community-centered solutions for enhancing that access. The study employed a qualitative case study design, integrating resilience theory with Goffman’s theory of stigma. Ten children from CHHs constituted the primary participants, while five key informants were purposively selected. The study generated data through in-depth and key informant interviews and analyzed them using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analysis. Findings indicated that CHH children experience trauma, chronic stress, anxiety, prolonged grief, and helplessness, with limited opportunities to communicate this distress. Access to mental health services was constrained by poverty, limited service availability, low mental health literacy, and a stigma in which disclosure is a communicative act carrying a lasting social cost. Proposed solutions centered on community-embedded communication channels: local service delivery, mental health education, free provision, coordinated multisectoral action, and mobile outreach modeled on familiar community health communication infrastructure.

title: Using extracorporeal ozone to treat experimental gram-negative sepsis: an exploratory study
abstractText: Abstract Background Sepsis is the third leading cause of death worldwide, yet there is a significant gap in the development of novel therapeutic approaches. Extracorporeal ozone has recently demonstrated beneficial effects in gram-negative sepsis (bactericidal and anti-inflammatory). We therefore evaluated extracorporeal ozone treatment in an experimental model of acute gram-negative sepsis to explore whether it improves clinically relevant outcomes. Methods Male and female pigs ( n = 9, 31 ± 2 kg) were used. Sepsis was induced by a 30-minute intravenous infusion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa , followed by an additional 30 min for sepsis development. Organ failure was classified according to SOFA score. The pigs were then assigned to either the untreated group ( n = 5) or the ozone-treated group ( n = 4). Treatment continued for 1 h (SangAsept™ system, O 2 /O 3 ratio 98:2%, 50 mL/min, 40 g/m 3 ). After treatment, the pigs were followed for an additional 2 h (endpoint). Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman’s rank correlation, and Fisher’s exact test were used for statistical analysis. Results The ozone-treated pigs had lower SOFA score than untreated pigs. The ozone-treated pigs maintained a normal mean arterial pressure without vasopressor support, whereas 80% of untreated pigs required vasopressor support. Hemoglobin levels remained within the normal range in the treated group but increased in the untreated group. Bilirubin levels were twofold higher in untreated pigs than in ozone-treated pigs. There was a significant positive correlation at endpoint between IL-6 and hemoglobin. Discussion In conclusion, this exploratory cohort of acute experimental gram-negative sepsis showed promising clinical outcomes after 1 h of extracorporeal ozone treatment, suggesting that this approach may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for sepsis.

KEMAMPUAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH MATEMATIKA MATERI VEKTOR DITINJAU DARI GAYA KOGNITIF
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematika materi vektor pada siswa kelas X SMA Muhammadiyah Sungguminasa ditinjau dari gaya kognitif Field Independent (FI) dan Field Dependent (FD). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas empat siswa yang dipilih secara purposif, yaitu satu siswa laki-laki dan satu siswa perempuan pada masing-masing kelompok FI dan FD. Data diperoleh melalui tes gaya kognitif, tes kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematika materi vektor, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Analisis data dilakukan berdasarkan empat tahap pemecahan masalah Polya, yaitu memahami masalah, menyusun rencana penyelesaian, melaksanakan rencana penyelesaian, dan memeriksa kembali hasil penyelesaian. Proses analisis data meliputi tiga tahapan, yaitu reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Pada tahap reduksi data, peneliti menyeleksi dan menyederhanakan data yang diperoleh dari hasil tes tertulis dan wawancara siswa sesuai dengan indikator pada setiap tahap pemecahan masalah Polya. Selanjutnya, pada tahap penyajian data, data disusun dan diuraikan secara sistematis dalam bentuk deskripsi untuk menggambarkan kemampuan siswa dalam memenuhi setiap tahap pemecahan masalah Polya. Tahap terakhir adalah penarikan kesimpulan, yaitu merumuskan hasil analisis berdasarkan data yang telah direduksi dan disajikan untuk mengetahui kemampuan siswa dalam menyelesaikan masalah matematika berdasarkan keempat tahap pemecahan masalah Polya. Perbaiki sesuai dengan revisi: Keabsahan data diperiksa melalui perbandingan hasil tes tertulis dan wawancara. Perbandingan ini dilakukan dengan mencocokkan jawaban tertulis siswa dengan informasi yang diperoleh melalui wawancara untuk mengetahui kesesuaian antara hasil pekerjaan dan penjelasan siswa. Dengan demikian, data yang diperoleh dapat memberikan gambaran yang lebih mendalam mengenai kemampuan siswa pada setiap tahap pemecahan masalah Polya.. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa subjek FI dan FD sama-sama mampu melalui tahap memahami masalah, menyusun rencana, melaksanakan rencana, dan memeriksa kembali. Subjek FI cenderung lebih rinci dalam memilih dan mengolah informasi yang relevan, sedangkan subjek FD cenderung mengolah informasi berdasarkan konteks permasalahan secara keseluruhan. Kedua kelompok mampu memperoleh hasil penyelesaian yang benar. Perbedaan terutama terlihat pada kelengkapan proses pemeriksaan kembali, karena subjek FD cenderung melakukan pemeriksaan secara lebih singkat. Dengan demikian, gaya kognitif memberikan gambaran mengenai karakteristik proses pemecahan masalah, tetapi tidak menjadi penentu tunggal keberhasilan siswa dalam menyelesaikan masalah vektor.

title: Penerapan Model Pembelajaran Kooperatif Tipe Think Pair Share dalam Meningkatkan Keaktifan Belajar Siswa di SMP Negeri 01 Tempurejo
abstractText: Keaktifan belajar siswa merupakan salah satu faktor penting yang menentukan keberhasilan proses pembelajaran. Namun, hasil observasi di SMP Negeri 01 Tempurejo menunjukkan bahwa keaktifan belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran IPS masih tergolong rendah karena pembelajaran cenderung berpusat pada guru sehingga siswa kurang berpartisipasi dalam bertanya, berdiskusi, maupun mengemukakan pendapat. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan model pembelajaran kooperatif tipe Think Pair Share (TPS) serta menganalisis peningkatan keaktifan belajar siswa setelah model tersebut diterapkan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) dengan model Kemmis dan McTaggart yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, masing-masing terdiri atas tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian adalah 27 siswa kelas VII SMP Negeri 01 Tempurejo Tahun Pelajaran 2025/2026. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif kuantitatif dan deskriptif kualitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model Think Pair Share mampu meningkatkan keaktifan belajar siswa pada setiap siklus. Persentase keaktifan belajar siswa meningkat dari 58,3% pada siklus I dengan kategori cukup baik menjadi 83,3% pada siklus II dengan kategori baik. Aktivitas guru juga mengalami peningkatan dari 75,0% pada siklus I menjadi 91,7% pada siklus II dengan kategori sangat baik. Peningkatan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa tahapan think, pair, dan share mampu mendorong siswa untuk berpikir secara mandiri, berdiskusi, berkomunikasi, serta berpartisipasi aktif dalam proses pembelajaran. Dengan demikian, model pembelajaran kooperatif tipe Think Pair Share terbukti efektif meningkatkan keaktifan belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran IPS di SMP Negeri 01 Tempurejo dan dapat dijadikan sebagai alternatif model pembelajaran yang mendukung pembelajaran aktif.

title: Wondering about war: the development of interest towards conflict through sequential knowledge acquisition
abstractText: Abstract Reminders of war are ubiquitous, capturing the living rooms, phone screens, and the interest of many. Although war media can be distressing, many consume it daily. Yet, we know little about how people’s initial engagement and interest in wars develops. Earlier studies found that early interest in neutral topics rises as knowledge is gathered and then eventually declines. In two studies ( N = 290), we examined whether interest in wars follows a similar pattern, hypothesizing that interest increases as knowledge accumulates, and then eventually drops. Participants could freely choose to read short Wikipedia-based texts about various wars. In addition, they reported their compassion toward those involved in each war. After each text, they rated their current interest in the conflict. Multilevel analyses supported our hypothesis, revealing both a positive linear and a negative quadratic effect of the amount of information read on interest, suggesting that interest grows with knowledge acquisition before tapering off. Additionally, compassion for those affected by a war positively predicted interest in that war. This study takes an initial step toward understanding how emotional responses shape early engagement with war media.

title: Layer pseudospin superconductivity in twisted MoTe2
abstractText: Recent experiments have observed signatures of spin-valley-polarized unconventional superconductivity in twisted bilayer MoTe 2 (tMoTe 2 ). Here, we explore the rich physics of superconducting tMoTe 2 , enabled by its unique layer-pseudospin structure. Within a minimal two-band model, both interlayer and intralayer Cooper pairings can be effectively visualized on a layer-space Bloch sphere. Importantly, we find that interlayer pairing dominates in the spin-valley-polarized state, while intralayer pairing prevails in the spin-valley-unpolarized state. We further predict that, for the spin-valley-polarized intravalley superconducting state, experimentally feasible weak displacement fields can stabilize finite-momentum pairing at low temperatures. Additionally, in-plane magnetic fields, which break three-fold rotational symmetry, induce field-direction-dependent finite-momentum pairing states, yielding a versatile momentum-selection diagram. Our work highlights the pivotal role of layer pseudospin in tMoTe 2 ’s unconventional superconductivity and demonstrates its unique tunability via external fields.

abstractText: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe2S2] and [Fe4S4] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems. The authors introduce a general framework that embeds exact spin symmetry directly into the neural network wavefunction, guaranteeing spin-pure states by construction. This design enables accurate resolution of near-degenerate spin states in challenging chemical systems.

title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
abstractText: Abstract We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $$\mathcal {G} \rightrightarrows M.$$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $$\mathcal {G} $$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of M . On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.

title: TSE-Net: Semi-supervised monocular height estimation from single remote sensing images
abstractText: Monocular height estimation plays a critical role in 3D perception for remote sensing, offering a cost-effective alternative to multi-view or LiDAR-based methods. While deep learning has significantly advanced the capabilities of monocular height estimation, these methods remain fundamentally limited by the availability of labeled data, which are expensive and labor-intensive to obtain at scale. The scarcity of high-quality annotations hinders the generalization and performance of existing models. To overcome this limitation, we propose leveraging large volumes of unlabeled data through a semi-supervised learning framework, enabling the model to extract informative cues from unlabeled samples and improve its predictive performance. In this work, we introduce Teacher-Student-Exam Network (TSE-Net), a self-training pipeline for semi-supervised monocular height estimation. The pipeline integrates teacher, student, and exam networks. The student network is trained on unlabeled data using pseudo-labels generated by the teacher network, while the exam network functions as a temporal ensemble of the student network to stabilize performance. The teacher network is formulated as a joint regression and classification model: the regression branch predicts height values that serve as pseudo-labels, and the classification branch predicts height value classes along with class probabilities, which are used to filter pseudo-labels. Height value classes are defined using a novel Hierarchical Bi-Cut (HBC) strategy to address the inherent long-tailed distribution of heights, and the predicted class probabilities are calibrated with a Plackett-Luce model to reflect the expected accuracy of pseudo-labels. We evaluate the proposed pipeline on three datasets spanning different resolutions and imaging modalities: the ISPRS Vaihingen dataset (IR-R-G aerial images, 0.09 m resolution), the SynRS3D dataset (synthetic images, 0.6–1 m resolution), and the GBH dataset (satellite RGB images, 3 m resolution). Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms supervised and semi-supervised baselines in low-label regimes, and ablation studies confirm the contribution and dataset-dependent behavior of each design component. Code is available at https://github.com/zhu-xlab/tse-net . • First self-training-based semi-supervised learning pipeline for monocular height estimation. • Teacher-Student-Exam pipeline with classification-regression teacher. • Hierarchical Bi-Cut reduces long-tailed biases in height predictions. • Plackett-Luce model aligns pseudo-label reliability with class confidence. • Up to 29.07% gap reduction between 100% and 0.1% labeled data.

title: Demographics-Informed Neural Network for Multimodal Spatiotemporal Forecasting of Urban Growth and Travel Patterns Using Satellite Imagery
abstractText: Abstract Transportation planning requires anticipating how built environments, population characteristics, and aggregate travel indicators evolve over time. Conventional forecasting approaches often treat these dimensions separately, limiting their ability to represent spatial-demographic change. This study introduces the Demographics-Informed Neural Network (DINN), a deep learning framework that forecasts next-year county-level satellite imagery from historical image sequences while enforcing demographic consistency through a frozen demographic predictor. DINN combines an encoder-decoder image predictor, gated skip connections, demographic bottleneck fusion, and demographic consistency regularization. The frozen demographic encoder is then reused as a fixed feature extractor to estimate aggregate county-level commute-mode and vehicle-availability indicators. Experiments using US county data from 2012 to 2023 show that DINN achieves an MSE of 0.00379 and SSIM of 0.8342 for satellite image prediction. Across repeated grouped spatial splits, DINN provides modest but consistent improvements over ConvLSTM, transformer-based, and encoder-decoder baselines, with stronger performance on both image reconstruction and change-detection metrics. The demographic predictor explains approximately 80% of the variance in population characteristics from satellite imagery. Transfer learning results show higher accuracy for absolute travel-indicator counts than for scale-controlled shares, indicating that part of the signal reflects county population scale. Overall, the findings suggest that satellite-derived spatial representations capture built-environment and demographic correlates of aggregate travel indicators; however, the results should be interpreted as county-level predictive associations rather than causal behavioral inference.

title: When active learning fails, uncalibrated out of distribution uncertainty quantification might be the problem
abstractText: Abstract Efficiently and meaningfully estimating prediction uncertainty is important for exploration in active learning campaigns in materials discovery, where samples with high uncertainty are interpreted as containing information missing from the model. In this work, the effect of different uncertainty estimation and calibration methods are evaluated for active learning when using ensembles of ALIGNN, eXtreme Gradient Boost, Random Forest, and Neural Network model architectures. We compare uncertainty estimates from ALIGNN deep ensembles to loss landscape uncertainty estimates obtained for solubility, bandgap, and formation energy prediction tasks. We then evaluate how the quality of the uncertainty estimate impacts an active learning campaign that seeks model generalization to out-of-distribution data. Uncertainty calibration methods were found to variably generalize from in-domain data to out-of-domain data. Furthermore, calibrated uncertainties were generally unsuccessful in reducing the amount of data required by a model to improve during an active learning campaign on out-of-distribution data when compared to random sampling and uncalibrated uncertainties. The impact of poor-quality uncertainty persists for random forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting models trained on the same data for the same tasks, indicating that this is at least partially intrinsic to the data and not due to model capacity alone. Analysis of the target, in-distribution uncertainty, out-of-distribution uncertainty, and training residual distributions suggest that future work focus on understanding empirical uncertainties in the feature input space for cases where ensemble prediction variances do not accurately capture the missing information required for the model to generalize.

title: Nuclear magnetic resonance on a single atom with a local probe
abstractText: Atomic nuclear spins are promising candidates in the development of quantum information technologies on a wide variety of physical platforms. Thanks to the high degree of isolation from their environment, nuclear spins show long-lived spin states, but this also poses challenges on their control and readability. Detailed characterization and control over the atomic-scale environment of the nuclear spin become of great importance for their efficient control. In this work, using scanning tunnelling microscopy, we reveal nuclear magnetic resonance on a single on-surface atom. We employ an electron-nuclear double resonance measurement scheme and resolve nuclear spin transitions of a single 47Ti isotope with a nuclear spin of I = 5/2. Our measurements and numerical analysis reveal the nature of hyperfine and quadrupole couplings of the studied system. We also show our ability to address the nuclear spin in the limit of weak hybridization with the electron spin, a requirement for direct control of the nuclear spin in the long-lifetime regime. This investigation of an atomic nuclear spin in a platform with atomic-scale control is a valuable development for other platforms deploying nuclear spins. Nuclear magnetic resonance of individual on-surface atoms has relied on electron-nuclear spin hybridization. Here, the authors use electron-nuclear double resonance with a scanning tunnelling microscope to resolve nuclear-spin transitions of a single atom on a surface in the weak-hybridization regime.

title: Isotopic Compositions and Source Identification of Atmospheric Particulate Bound Cadmium in Chinese Megacities
abstractText: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) bound cadmium (Cd) deposition on the Earth's surface poses significant ecological risks to humans and the environment. Cd stable isotopes are useful tracers for understanding sources and biogeochemical cycling in the Earth's ecosystems, yet knowledge of atmospheric Cd isotopic compositions remains limited. Here we present measurements of Cd isotopic compositions in fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) in five megacities selected to represent different anthropogenic Cd emission structures across China and explore potential atmospheric Cd sources. The mean (±1 SD) δ 114 Cd values of PM 2.5 were −0.231 ± 0.520‰, −0.192 ± 0.265‰, −0.003 ± 0.167‰, 0.005 ± 0.089‰, and 0.090 ± 0.121‰ in Chengdu, Lanzhou, Guangzhou, Jinan, and Beijing, respectively, more negative than δ 114 Cd signatures in the global remote atmosphere. Anticorrelations between δ 114 Cd and anthropogenic emission tracers (i.e., PM 2.5 ‐bound Cd concentrations and enrichment factors), and high Cd/As ratios in Chengdu and Lanzhou, indicate anthropogenic atmospheric Cd emissions mainly from nonferrous metal smelting. No such relationship was observed in other cities, where the δ 114 Cd and Cd/As ratios indicate coal‐fired emissions. Overall, the results of our study suggest that compared with the remote atmosphere, both coal combustion and nonferrous metal smelting cause a shift in PM 2.5 ‐bound Cd toward lighter isotopic compositions, with nonferrous metal smelting characterized by significantly more negative δ 114 Cd values and higher Cd/As ratios. Combined with Cd/As ratios, Cd isotopes provide a promising tool for identifying major anthropogenic atmospheric Cd sources.
