title: The N−5 scaling law: Topological dimensionality reduction in the optimal design of fully-actuated multirotors
abstractText: We investigate the topological structure of the optimal actuation landscape for fully-actuated N -rotor aerial vehicles. By formulating the design problem on the 2 N -dimensional product manifold of projective lines ( R P 2 ) N and minimizing a rotation-invariant Log-Volume isotropy metric, we map how optimal rotor orientations evolve across diverse polyhedral chassis. The results establish that global optimality is strictly bounded by geometric symmetry. While irregular chassis yield discrete, isolated optimal configurations, regular geometries induce a structural phase transition: the optimal space initially collapses onto an N -dimensional Tangent Torus, then systematically reduces to continuous configurations governed by affine phase coordination. These collapses define the “ N −5 Scaling Law.” For N ≤ 7, the optimal landscape fundamentally forms exactly K = N −5 disconnected 1D closed loops. For N ≥ 8, these 1D trajectories expand into core backbones embedded within multi-dimensional flat optimal hypersurfaces. Furthermore, for regular planar geometries, we theoretically unify these trajectories by demonstrating a strict geometric isomorphism to star polygons { N / q } (2 < q < N − 2), yielding exact analytical predictions of the N −5-branched optimal manifolds for arbitrary N . By shifting the classical framework from single and static optimal points to continuous optimal manifolds, this work establishes the mathematical foundations for optimality-preserving morphing. The identified topological branches provide continuous null spaces, introducing to the field the concept of design redundancy , and allowing symmetric multirotor systems to dynamically reconfigure their thrust vectors without degrading their perfectly isotropic control authority.

title: Risk Minimisation Communication in Non-EU Countries
abstractText: Communicating risk and safety information to patients and healthcare professionals is a public health and our ethical responsibility. Risk communication is central to risk management strategy of pharmaceutical companies. This way will be achieved the objectives of pharmacovigilance in terms of promoting the rational, safe and effective use of medicinal products. It is imperative in the pharmaceutical sector and industry, preventing occurrence and harm of adverse drug and medical reactions, minimising risks, which leads to protection of the patients and public health. In this article we will elaborate the risk and risk minimisation communication. Countries of interest are North Macedonia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania and Kosovo, making comparison with the European Union (EU). Risk minimisation communication should enhance awareness of patients/caregivers on careful monitoring, early detection and steps to be taken in order to achieve the safe use of medicinal products. The objectives of ensuring the safe use of the medicinal product and minimising risks, including their adverse health outcomes are facilitated by risk minimisation measures (RMMs). We will give an in depth look at regulation compliance from the markets of interest within country-specific environments.

title: Photonic Neuromorphic Processing With Coupled Spiking Silicon Microrings
abstractText: ABSTRACT Understanding the physical computing mechanisms of individual network nodes is essential for scaling neuromorphic photonic architectures. This work proposes a compact passive nonlinear photonic core based on a side‐coupled integrated spaced sequence of resonators (SCISSOR) comprising three nominally equal microrings and investigate its computing capabilities. Its nonlinearities and internal feedback enable analogue, spiking, and bistable responses that are accessed by tuning the injection power and wavelength. Implemented as a single nonlinear node in a time‐multiplexed reservoir computing, the SCISSOR achieves error‐free classification on the Iris dataset and accuracies above 97 on the Sonar task, using both analogue and digital reservoir representations with 150 virtual nodes. In the digital scheme, spiking dynamics naturally generate sparse reservoir states, enabling efficient classification even with a single spike. Intriguingly, operating points at the boundaries where sharp transitions in dynamical complexity and/or output power occur support high task‐performance, opening novel strategies for future on‐chip training. Spiking and thermal bistabilities also participate to enhance the computational performance. These results suggest that coupled optical microrings can serve as compact, physically interpretable nonlinear building blocks for future neuromorphic photonic processors, particularly in optical‐domain preprocessing and sensing scenarios where kHz‐to‐MHz signal bandwidths are relevant.

title: On some problems regarding LCM-groups
abstractText: Let G be a finite group and denote by o(g) the order of an element g∈G. We say that G is an LCM-group if o(xny) is a divisor of the least common multiple of o(xn) and o(y) for all x,y∈G and n∈N. This paper extends some existing results on LCM-groups, such as the structure of a minimal non-LCM-group, and establishes criteria for G to be an LCM-group or a nilpotent group. We also prove that, in general, a minimum cover of a finite set of LCM-groups is not an LCM-group, and we answer two questions posed by M. Amiri.

title: Oscillons from Q-balls in generalized models
abstractText: We study the oscillon/$Q$-ball relation in an extended model with non-canonical kinematics. The model contains a single real scalar field whose kinetic term is enlarged to include a generalizing function. We approximate the real sector up to the third order in a book-keeping parameter. In this context, we implement the Renormalization Group Perturbation Expansion (RGPE), from which we conclude that the relation between oscillons and underlying $Q$-balls holds even in the presence of nontrivial kinematics. We apply our results to the study of three different effective cases. In all of them, our expressions mimic the numerical evolution of nonstandard oscillons with great accuracy, especially for small and moderate amplitudes. As the initial amplitude increases, the numerical profile develops a modulated behavior, and we use a two $Q$-balls solution to seed our analytical oscillon. We discuss how our non-canonical construction allows the existence of a well-behaved oscillon in connection to the simplest $ϕ^2$-potential. This novel profile behaves in the same general way as the previous ones. So, we argue that they belong to the same universality class. Finally, we extend our analysis to consider those contributions up to the fifth order in the approximation expansion. We explore an exotic $ϕ^6$-scenario, and conclude that the relation between generalized oscillons and underlying $Q$-balls now belongs to a different universality class.

title: Profilaxia pré-exposição ao HIV em populações de maior vulnerabilidade: revisão de escopo
abstractText: Objetivo: Mapear as estratégias de Profilaxia Pré-Exposição (PrEP) ao HIV em populações de maior vulnerabilidade e identificar o papel do farmacêutico no acesso e adesão. Métodos: Revisão de escopo conduzida segundo o Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI), utilizando o acrônimo PCC (Participantes: serviços de distribuição/dispensação de PrEP; Conceito: PrEP ao HIV; Contexto: populações vulneráveis). Buscas realizadas em Lilacs, PubMed, SciELO, Cochrane, JBI Evidence Synthesis, ScienceDirect, CAPES e Google Acadêmico, com recorte de 2021 a 2026. Os estudos foram gerenciados no Mendeley® e selecionados no Rayyan®. Resultados: Foram incluídos 19 artigos. A maioria apresentou nível de evidência muito baixo (57,9%). Apenas 3 estudos (15,7%) abordaram o papel do farmacêutico, evidenciando lacuna na literatura. Os fatores socioeconômicos, estigma, escolaridade e raça foram os principais determinantes para o acesso e adesão à PrEP. Considerações finais: A PrEP é estratégia efetiva, mas barreiras estruturais e sociais limitam seu alcance em populações vulneráveis. A atuação farmacêutica é promissora, porém pouco explorada, demandando estudos mais robustos e políticas públicas inclusivas.

title: Discovery of Potent and Non-cytotoxic HDAC3-Selective Degraders Featuring a Propyl Hydrazide Zinc-Binding Group
abstractText: Abstract Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is an important therapeutic target in cancer, yet selective HDAC3 degraders remain limited. In this study, we report the development of novel class I HDAC degraders derived from the HDAC3-preferential inhibitor FL-007. Two linker exit vectors were investigated, leading to the identification of a series of potent compounds (2a−d) exhibiting low micromolar inhibition of HDAC2 and submicromolar inhibition of HDAC1 and HDAC3, together with selective HDAC3 degradation. Degradation activity was confirmed in MM.1S, HCT116, A2780-HDAC3-HiBiT, and Cal27CisR cells using immunoblotting and HiBiT/LgBiT assays, achieving Dmax values of up to 92%. Notably, these compounds showed no cytotoxicity up to 100 μM in both cancerous and non-cancerous cell lines. Selective HDAC3 degradation resulted in moderate chemosensitization of cisplatin-resistant Cal27CisR cells, in contrast to the stronger effects observed with cytotoxic HDAC inhibitors. For compound 2b, the chemosensitizing effect was associated with increased histone H3 acetylation and increased p21 expression.

title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
abstractText: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy. Using human brain organoids, here authors report that GATOR1 loss impairs GABAergic interneurons via MAFB downregulation, independently of mTOR hyperactivation, offering new mechanistic insights into genetic focal epilepsy.

title: Using colours to assess the intensity of emotions and pain: a validation of two coloured visual analogue scales
abstractText: Visual Analogue Scales (VAS) are widely used in clinical and research settings to measure subjective experiences. Coloured versions (Colour Analogue Scales - CAS) have been proposed for emotions in specific samples such as children and people suffering from cognitive deficits. To date, data on the comparability of the two types of measures are meagre. The present study fills this gap by recording the perceived intensity of emotions and pain experienced by healthy adults ( N = 128, mean age = 21.64 ± 3.36, 62 females, 66 males). In Experiment 1, the participants rated the valence of emotions in human faces using a VAS and a coloured scale (E-CAS), with yellow representing happiness and blue grey representing sadness. In Experiment 2, they rated the imaginary pain intensity typically associated with certain daily life situations, in this case using a VAS and a red-shaded CAS. The results from the two scales were compared. Convergent and concurrent validity were assessed in correlation analyses, while construct validity was examined using repeated-measures analyses. Response times were compared to evaluate the potential effects of format. High correlations and comparable sensitivity were found between the CAS and VAS scales. Crucially, responses to the coloured scales were faster than the VAS, suggesting a reduced cognitive load in their use, that makes them potentially indicated for patients with cognitive deficits.

title: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
abstractText: Abstract Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance and not the full transport process. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. This limitation is especially relevant in realistic multiphase, structured, and time-dependent media, and is also reflected in observed environmental variations in CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants, and molecular clouds. Particle-tracing studies also show clear departures from standard diffusion, including both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on P(x, t), the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier–Laplace transform P(k, s). This object is compact and statistically complete, and naturally exposes memory: the CR flux can depend on earlier gradients when unresolved trapping or phase changes are coarse-grained away. Using the Montroll–Weiss formalism, we show how to measure P(k, s) directly from trajectories, how to recover the associated memory kernel, and how to represent broad kernels efficiently with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence-time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, and show that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This paper provides the foundation for future observational applications, particle-tracing measurements, and CR-MHD closures.

title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event
abstractText: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations. Using astrochronology, Wang et al. estimate that relative sea-level change led benthic turnover by ~70,000 years during the late Cambrian SPICE event under their age model, supporting links among orbital forcing, marine anoxia and biodiversity loss.

title: Duality of Hamiltonian and Lagrangian Formulations for Integrable Systems
abstractText: Abstract We introduce the concept of Hamiltonian potential variables to map Hamiltonian operators into symplectic operators in a dual space. This generalises the classical trick of switching to a potential variable to obtain a Lagrangian density for the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation. Building on this concept, we present the Lagrangian structure for bi-Hamiltonian systems, discuss the Lenard scheme in the symplectic formalisms, and apply this to construct pairs of Lagrangian multiforms. We discuss the key model of the KdV equation and some dispersionless limits of it. We present a pair of Lagrangian multiforms for these equations, one of which is new. We also consider the examples of polytropic gas dynamics and the constant astigmatism equation, for which no Lagrangian multiforms were previously known.

title: Evidence map of mixed reality as templates in orthognathic surgery: a scoping review
abstractText: Abstract Background This scoping review mapped the use of mixed reality and augmented reality (MR/AR) as intraoperative navigation-transfer templates in orthognathic surgery. PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 19 September 2026, supplemented by a manual/citation search; screening and data charting were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third. Results Searches identified 364 records (363 from databases, 1 via citation searching); after removing 13 duplicates and screening 350 records, 23 reports were sought for retrieval (0 not retrieved) and assessed for eligibility, of which 3 were excluded. Twenty studies were included (19 from databases, 1 from citation searching; 12 clinical and 8 preclinical/phantom studies). MR/AR was used mainly for osteotomy-line transfer, maxillary or mandibular segment repositioning, occlusion verification, and plate or patient-specific implant (PSI) fixation. Optical-see-through head-mounted displays, especially HoloLens or HoloLens 2, were the most frequently reported platform, and marker-based registration predominated over markerless teeth- or surface-matching approaches. Reported accuracy varied by error type and workflow task and is presented separately for registration/tracking error, surface-distance error and postoperative repositioning error rather than as a single pooled range. Twelve of 20 studies were single-arm accuracy studies assessed only against a reference standard (planned virtual surgical plan vs. postoperative imaging), and 8 of 20 included a concurrent comparator arm. Conclusions MR/AR is used mainly as an intraoperative adjunct for transferring the virtual surgical plan in orthognathic surgery. The available evidence suggests technical feasibility and generally sub-millimetre-to-2 mm deviations under favourable conditions, but remains heterogeneous and dominated by small, early-phase, largely single-arm studies; it should not be read as a validated or pooled accuracy estimate. Well-designed comparative studies with standardized, clinically anchored outcome thresholds are still needed.

title: Quantitative modelling of type Ia supernovae spectral time series II:Exploring the diversity of thermonuclear explosion scenarios
abstractText: Abstract Observations of type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) have led to suggestions of multiple progenitor and explosion scenarios. Distinguishing between scenarios and tying specific SNe Ia to individual scenarios however has so far been challenging. Constraints on the explosion physics are often achieved through empirical modelling of SNe Ia spectra and qualitative assessments of the level of agreement. While this approach has provided useful insights, it cannot be scaled up to large numbers of SNe Ia in a robust and systematic way. riddler is a machine learning based framework for automated and quantitative fitting of SNe Ia designed to overcome these limitations. Neural networks are used as radiative transfer emulators and, in conjunction with nested sampling, emulated spectra are fit to observations of SNe Ia to determine the best-fitting input parameters and explosion scenario. In this work, we present recent improvements to riddler, including a significantly expanded training dataset covering pure deflagrations, delayed detonations, double detonations, gravitationally confined detonations, and violent mergers. We show that despite the increased complexity and variety of our training data, riddler is able to accurately recover the input parameters and explosion scenario of spectra unseen during training. Using riddler, we fit observations of three SNe Ia covering different sub-classes: SN 2011fe, SN 2005hk, and SN 2018byg. We detail a number of limitations and assumptions that should be considered when applying similar approaches. Nevertheless, the benefits of this approach and riddler will result in automated fitting playing an increasingly important role in the coming years.

Effect of RANDALLfoils on the fluid dynamics of rowing
abstractText: Abstract Rowing-blade attachments have the potential to modify blade-fluid interactions during the rowing stroke, however these effects remain difficult to isolate in on-water rowing. This study experimentally investigates the RANDALLfoil, a blade attachment designed to alter the flow around a rowing blade, using 1:4 scaled rowing motions. Force and torque measurements are collected for a standard blade and a RANDALLfoil blade, and two-dimensional particle image velocimetry (PIV) is used to relate the measured loading to leading-edge vortex (LEV) development. For the representative scaled motion, the RANDALLfoil increased propulsive impulse ( $$J_x$$ ) by 9.01% and impulse efficiency ( $$\eta _J$$ ) by 4.91%, indicating greater momentum transfer in the direction of boat motion and a response consistent with reduced blade slip. Whilst the total integrated pitching torque had negligible difference over the duration of the stroke, the pitching torque of the blade was consistently lower in the first half of the stroke for the RANDALLfoil. PIV results showed that changes in blade-normal force were not explained by LEV circulation magnitude alone. Instead, the force response was better interpreted using circulation magnitude, circulation-growth rate, LEV area, and vortex-core distance from the blade. These results suggest that the RANDALLfoil modifies blade loading by changing both LEV development and blade-vortex coupling during the drive. This study was limited to the submerged drive phase of the rowing stroke at 1:4 scaled geometry and a reduced Reynolds number from full-scale rowing. PIV measurements were performed at the mid-height of the blade so three-dimensional flow structures were not captured.

title: Do consumer-facing “Indica,” “Sativa,” and “Hybrid” labels predict cannabis composition or effects? A systematic review
abstractText: Abstract Background Consumer- and patient-facing cannabis products are commonly labeled “indica,” “sativa,” or “hybrid” to signal expected composition or effects. We systematically reviewed whether these labels predict cannabis composition, animal effects, or human outcomes. Methods We last searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, PubPsych, OpenAlex, and ClinicalTrials.gov, supplemented by Elicit coverage checking and citation searching; records were then screened for peer-reviewed empirical reports published from June 1, 2011, through June 1, 2026. Eligible reports directly compared consumer-facing indica, sativa, or hybrid labels, or included such labels in statistical/model-based analyses. Methodological concern and evidence directness were appraised using stream-specific domains. Results Twenty-eight peer-reviewed reports were included: 12 plant/product-database/composition reports, one animal marketed-preparation report, and 15 human treatment, symptom-relief, or proximal-outcome reports. Plant/product reports showed limited concordance between labels and genetic structure or major cannabinoid profiles. Terpene findings were compound-specific and inconsistent, with some label-associated signals but no stable label-to-terpene rule. The animal report described preparation-specific cognitive-effort differences between two oils marketed as indica or sativa. Across human reports, label associations with symptom relief, subjective effects, behavioral or neurophysiological outcomes, and side effects were inconsistent. Significant associations were reported for selected outcomes, including insomnia relief and low-arousal effects, but adjustment for delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content and other potential confounders varied. Comparisons without THC adjustment could not establish whether label-associated outcome differences were independent of differences in product potency. Conclusions The evidence does not support using indica, sativa, and hybrid labels as reliable guides to cannabis composition or therapeutic effects. More defensible descriptors include measured chemistry, product form, route, dose, and patient-specific safety considerations. Current terpene-effect evidence remains preliminary and does not justify terpene-based or label-based prescribing rules. title: Length Scale Coordination Between Effective Electron Diffusion and Light‐Emitting Boosts Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency
abstractText: ABSTRACT Electrochemiluminescence (ECL), the emission of light excited by electrochemical reactions, has drawn attention as a powerful tool for bioassays and environmental monitoring. Nonetheless, a limited understanding of the bulk electron transport (ET) process in solid‐state ECL emitters, particularly the mismatch between the electron diffusion length ( L n ) at the photoelectrode and the light‐emitting layer thickness ( d ), significantly undermines the ECL efficiency ( Φ ECL ) and impedes practical applications. Herein, we report L n /d as a quantitative impedance‐derived kinetic‐matching descriptor of bulk electron transport in solid‐state ECL systems, and an empirical L n / d range (0.9–1.2) for achieving high ECL efficiency is identified from the slope behavior of temporal ECL evolution curves. This strategy was further confirmed experimentally across different ECL systems, including metal‐organic frameworks (MOF), poly(heptazine imide) (PHI), and carbon nitride with tunable band structures. The optimal L n / d ratio range enabled superior electron transport and mass transfer, yielding a record‐high cathodic ECL efficiency for carbon nitride (CN) and enabling a visual tetracycline (TC) sensor with an excellent detection range and limit.

Can DFT-Trained Neural Network Potentials Reproduce Structure, Solvation, and Water-Exchange Properties in Aqueous Magnesium Solutions?
abstractText: Abstract Magnesium ions play an essential role in many biological processes but remain challenging to model in biomolecular simulations. Despite considerable scientific effort, classical force fields fail to simultaneously reproduce key structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic solution properties, likely due to their inability to explicitly account for quantum many-body effects. Here, we develop and systematically benchmark MACE neural network potentials (NNPs) for aqueous MgCl2 solutions, trained on revPBE-D3/zd and revPBE0-D3/zd density functional theory reference data, and assess their ability to reproduce a broad range of experimental solution properties including the structure of the first hydration shell, diffusion coefficient, activity derivative, water-exchange rate, and mechanism as well as solvation free energy. Both NNPs accurately reproduce the octahedral structure of the first hydration shell, ion-pairing properties, and diffusion coefficients. Combining the NNPs with transition path sampling and other enhanced sampling techniques allows us to capture the rare event of water exchange in the first hydration shell of Mg2+, revealing a dissociative exchange mechanism. Transition interface sampling yields exchange rates within 1 order of magnitude of experiment, representing a substantial improvement over classical dissociative force fields. In contrast, the NNP-derived solvation free energy significantly underestimates the experimental value, revealing a limitation of the present local NNP architecture for describing ion solvation thermodynamics. Our results demonstrate that DFT-trained NNPs can accurately describe Mg2+ hydration structure, diffusion, ion pairing, and exchange kinetics while highlighting limitations of local NNP architectures and the importance of long-range electrostatic contributions to achieve quantitative agreement with experimental ion solvation free energies.

title: On the contact of surfaces in 4-space with 2-planes and their apparent contours
abstractText: Abstract We investigate the local geometry of generic smooth surfaces in $$\mathbb R^4$$ R 4 through their contact with 2-planes and the associated apparent contour. We study the $$\mathcal A$$ A -singularities of parallel projections of such surfaces along planes to transverse planes. When the projection plane does not contain an asymptotic direction, we show that hyperbolic and elliptic points (respectively, parabolic points) admit up to ten (respectively, seven) tangent directions determining planes for which the projection has $$\mathcal A$$ A -singularities of type butterfly or worse. We also prove that the locus of points where the discriminant of the equation defining these directions vanishes generically forms regular curves in the hyperbolic and elliptic regions, and isolated points in the parabolic set. When the projection plane contains an asymptotic direction, we relate the singularities of parallel projections to those of orthogonal projections onto hyperplanes and height functions. We then investigate the associated apparent contour. When the projection is a fold, we establish a Mannheim–d’Ocagne–Koenderink-type theorem relating the Lipschitz–Killing curvature of the surface to the curvature of the apparent contour. We further show that elliptic and inflection points give rise to vertices of the apparent contour, whereas hyperbolic and parabolic points generate inflections. In the non-fold case, we prove that the apparent contour admits $$(t^k,t^\ell )$$ ( t k , t ℓ ) -cusp singularities associated with the singularities of the projection.

title: Temperature distribution measurement on three-phase contact line in liquid nitrogen using two-color temperature-sensitive paint
abstractText: Cryogenic phase-change phenomena play an important role in a wide range of engineering applications, including cryogenic cooling systems, superconducting technologies, and space propulsion systems. In particular, the three-phase contact line is recognized as a key region governing evaporation and heat transfer. However, direct measurements of temperature distributions near cryogenic three-phase contact lines remain limited because conventional infrared thermography becomes increasingly difficult at extremely low temperatures. In this study, a two-color temperature-sensitive paint (2C-TSP) technique was applied to visualize the temperature field around a liquid‑nitrogen three-phase contact line. A temperature-sensitive dye and a temperature-insensitive reference dye were incorporated into a single coating, enabling robust temperature measurements based on luminescence intensity ratios by compensating for changes in optical intensity caused by refraction and reflection at the liquid–gas interface. Temperature distributions were measured under three heating conditions with heat fluxes of 1.1 × 10 2 , 4.3 × 10 2 , and 9.0 × 10 2 W / m 2 . The measured temperature fields revealed a localized temperature minimum at the observed three-phase contact line, suggesting localized cooling associated with phase change. Quantitative analysis showed that the average temperature in the liquid region remained nearly constant, whereas the temperature in the gas region increased with increasing heat flux. These observations reveal a non-uniform thermal structure around the cryogenic three-phase contact line. The present results demonstrate that 2C-TSP is a promising technique for direct visualization of temperature fields around cryogenic three-phase contact lines and provides new insights into phase-change phenomena in liquid nitrogen.

title: A gauge-theoretic formulation of Nambu non-equilibrium thermodynamics
abstractText: We present a gauge-theoretic formulation of Nambu non-equilibrium thermodynamics (NNET) within a common gauge-fixed worldline framework. In this formulation, the generalized thermodynamic force is described by an Abelian thermodynamic connection, and ordinary Onsager dynamics is recovered by fixing its temporal component through the dissipation function. To extend this construction to NNET, we introduce a closed two-form as additional geometric input. This form determines a divergence-free Nambu vector field and thereby defines a characteristic direction on the extended thermodynamic state space. The Onsager gauge condition is then generalized so that the dissipative gauge fixing is imposed along this Nambu characteristic direction. The resulting constitutive relation reproduces the basic NNET evolution equation, combining nondissipative Nambu circulation with dissipative Onsager relaxation. We further show that the localized BF-type expression is not an independent pre-gauge-fixed action, but a differential-form representation of the Nambu-adapted gauge-fixed worldline theory. The Faddeev–Popov operator associated with the BRST gauge fixing becomes, on shell, the negative of the material derivative along the full NNET flow, and its time-independent zero-mode profiles satisfy the same equation as first integrals of the deterministic dynamics. Finite residual transformations obey a Hamilton–Jacobi equation governed by the same Onsager tensor, implying that the gauge parameter is nonincreasing along the original NNET flow. These results provide a unified geometric interpretation of Onsager dissipation and Nambu dynamics within a single gauge-fixing framework.

title: Transitioning from Glassware to Plasticware in an Industrial Analytical Laboratory Following a Laceration Incident: A Case Study
abstractText: Abstract Glassware-related lacerations are the most frequent category of injury in chemistry laboratories. Despite this, manual dishwashing, a daily routine step in every analytical laboratory, is virtually absent from safety literature as a distinct risk context. Here, we report a case study from an incident at the quality control laboratory of Saipol (Groupe Avril), a major European oilseed processing company, where a laboratory technician sustained a hand laceration requiring three sutures following the breakage of a glass beaker during postanalytical rinsing. Internally, glass cuts were identified as the most frequent accident type across Groupe Avril laboratories over the past ten years. The technician was wearing nitrile laboratory gloves at the time of the incident. A root cause analysis identified two contributing factors: water accumulation on the outer surface of the beaker reducing grip, and an instinctive catch reflex that forced the technician’s hand against the shattering glass. Following the NIOSH hierarchy of controls, a material substitution program was then implemented. A glassware use inventory (∼300 items/week) and a chemical compatibility assessment revealed that over 50% of glass items used mainly for titrimetric applications could be substituted with plastic equivalents (like poly(ethylene terephthalate glycol)-modified, polypropylene, and polymethylpentene). Comparative analyses confirmed no measurable analytical interference from the newly introduced PETG vessels. Consequently, based on item counts, the substitution achieved a 30% reduction in glassware usage (∼90 plastic items/week) across the facility over the past two years. This case study provides a transferable framework (inventory, compatibility evaluation, material selection, analytical validation, and implementation) for analytical laboratories seeking to reduce glassware-related injury risk.

title: Characterization of the Trimeric TOM Complex by HS ‐ AFM Single‐Molecule Analysis
abstractText: ABSTRACT The translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane (TOM) complex is the entry gate for mitochondrial proteins synthesized in the cytosol. Previous biochemical studies indicated that the TOM complex functions as a trimer and exists in a dynamic equilibrium with a Tom22‐lacking dimer in intact mitochondria. In contrast, recent cryo‐electron microscopy (cryo‐EM) studies revealed near‐atomic structures of the Tom22‐containing core dimer. However, the relationship between the core dimer and the functional trimer remains unclear. Here, we analyzed the oligomeric organization and structural properties of purified yeast TOM complexes using high‐speed atomic force microscopy (HS‐AFM). Purified yeast TOM complexes predominantly adopted a trimeric organization but underwent deformation and dissociation during repeated HS‐AFM scanning, leaving dimeric and monomeric particles. Trimeric particles exhibited spherical shapes consistent with previous crosslinking models, whereas dissociated dimers closely resembled TOM core‐dimer structures determined by cryo‐EM. HS‐AFM also revealed the peripheral localization of the Tom20 receptor and enabled direct visualization of substrate–TOM interactions, with TOM association accompanied by reduced substrate mobility. Together, these findings provide quantitative and structural evidence for a predominantly trimeric organization of the purified TOM complex and suggest that the trimer contains a stable core‐dimer unit with a more loosely associated third Tom40‐containing unit.

title: Basis‐Independent Geometric Phase Modulation in Circularly Birefringent Plasmonic Structures
abstractText: ABSTRACT Geometric phase in metasurfaces is conventionally realized using spatially rotated linearly birefringent meta–atoms under circularly polarized illumination. Here we demonstrate that a geometric phase modulation can be achieved through circular birefringence and observed under linear polarization excitation. We introduce a plasmonic metasurface composed of spatially rotated chiral spiral unit cells designed to produce space‐variant circular retardance. This generates a geometric phase ramp equivalent to a blazed grating, leading to diffraction orders in momentum space. Using leakage radiation microscopy, we directly resolve these orders and show how their intensities depend upon the input linear polarization confirming the geometric origin of the phase. We theoretically analyze the phenomenon using a rotated Poincaré space and confirm our results by direct Stokes parameters measurement. These results establish basis‐independent approach to geometric phase accumulation in circularly birefringent plasmonic metasurfaces.

title: Laser Power Transmission in Space: Plasma-Based Power Cell
abstractText: Abstract Laser power beaming offers a route to space energy delivery, but semiconductor laser photovoltaic receivers face thermalization, Joule heating, and radiative recombination losses at the solid-state junction. Here, we propose a gas-phase plasma power cell that converts incident vacuum-ultraviolet photons directly into electrical output through xenon photoionization, magnetically guided electron transport, and collection at a biased electrode surface, replacing the fixed semiconductor junction with an optically tunable, all-gas-phase energy-conversion medium. The model includes secondary electron emission at the electrode surfaces as a possible interfacial energy recycling pathway. Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulations of a low-pressure xenon chamber driven by a 58.4 nm pulsed laser predict a steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency of 82.25% at an average incident power of 2000 W/m. Energy accounting is close to 1%, with 7.52% photon escape, 8.95% boundary loss, and 1.29% chamber-stored energy. Parameter scans over bias voltage, magnetic field, and gas pressure identify photon absorption, electron confinement, and plasma-electrode charge collection as the controlling design factors. Because the present calculation is a preliminary numerical proof of concept using simplified kinetics and idealized surface, boundary, and energy-recycling treatments, the 82.25% value should be interpreted as a receiver-side model prediction conditional on those assumptions, rather than as a demonstrated or guaranteed device efficiency. These results establish a proof-of-concept gas-phase photonic receiver architecture for wireless laser power transmission in space.

title: Non-Ensemble, Conformation-Resolved Stability Analysis of Trispecific Antibodies by Differential Melting Voltage
abstractText: Abstract Trispecific antibodies (TriAbs) integrate multiple antigen-binding modules within a single construct, creating greater architectural complexity and conformational heterogeneity than conventional monoclonal antibodies. Conventional stability measurements report ensemble-averaged behavior and may therefore conceal stability differences among distinct conformational subpopulations within a TriAbs construct. Here, tandem-trapped ion mobility spectrometry (Tandem-TIMS) was combined with differential melting voltage (DMV) analysis to investigate the conformation-resolved gas-phase stability of wild-type and Fc-mutated TriAbs. Under native conditions, both antibody constructs retained compact, native-like structures with nearly identical ensemble-level cross sections. Nonensemble Tandem-TIMS measurements resolved distinct conformational subpopulations that followed different activation-induced unfolding trajectories, confirming that they represented structurally distinct conformational states. DMV analysis quantified these differences using a single, quantifiable metric: the melting voltage, Vm. The wild-type construct showed a stepwise increase in the melting voltage, with several conformational subpopulations displaying comparable relative stability toward collisional activation. In contrast, the AAS-mutated construct exhibited a more gradual increase in stability with increasing cross section. These differences were not apparent from the ensemble-level cross section distributions and were only weakly reflected in solution-phase nanoDSF measurements. The results demonstrate that similar intact antibody size and bulk thermal properties do not necessarily imply similar conformational landscapes. Most importantly, the integration of Tandem-TIMS with DMV analysis provides a nonensemble strategy for directly connecting structural heterogeneity with the relative gas-phase stability of conformational subpopulations in complex antibody therapeutics.

title: Relative Cohomology and Deformations of Logarithmic Foliations on Complex Spaces
abstractText: Abstract We study relative cohomology for logarithmic differential forms and meromorphic forms that are relatively closed with respect to the associated logarithmic foliation. Under suitable Diophantine, geometric, and topological hypotheses, we obtain decompositions into a meromorphic multiple of the defining logarithmic form, an exact meromorphic form, and a logarithmic form with constant residues. We establish a meromorphic extension theorem from suitable two-dimensional sections and prove local, polynomial, and homogeneous versions of the relative-cohomology decomposition; the global polynomial result is proved in arbitrary dimension by ambient leafwise continuation and meromorphic extension. Resolution of singularities, non-nodal saturation, and holonomy gluing are used to treat singular logarithmic foliations. As an application, we derive formal normal forms for analytic integrable deformations, including a several-component result in dimension two and a two-component extension in higher dimensions.

title: Multi-dimensional NLTE radiative transfer for a double detonation Type Ia explosion model in the photospheric phase
abstractText: Abstract Previous radiative transfer calculations have shown that both multi-dimensionality and NLTE (non local thermodynamic equilibrium) effects impact the synthetic observables predicted for Type Ia supernova explosion models. Here we carry out a 2D NLTE radiative transfer simulation in the photospheric phase for a double detonation model with a 1 M⊙ carbon–oxygen core and 0.02 M⊙ helium shell. The predicted observables demonstrate that departures from both spherical symmetry and local thermodynamic equilibrium are significant on scales relevant to comparisons with observations. The NLTE treatment leads to a bluer spectral energy distribution, more slowly declining optical-band light curves, changes to the near-infrared light curve shapes, and differences in the evolution of key spectral features. Although substantial viewing-angle variation is predicted for the model, the scale of the variation is not significantly impacted by NLTE effects up to peak. However, after peak, our 2D NLTE simulation retains a strong viewing-angle dependence in its spectra whereas our simulation of the same ejecta model using an approximate NLTE treatment predicts significantly reduced spectroscopic viewing-angle variation. The NLTE treatment leads to improved agreement with normal Type Ia supernovae, primarily due to the increased ionisation state of the simulation, although the absence of a secondary near-infrared maximum suggests that the ejecta remain over-ionised relative to observations after peak. Despite the improved agreement, many viewing angles still show excessive line blanketing, suggesting that the 0.02 M⊙ helium-shell mass of the current model is too large to reproduce normal Type Ia supernovae over the majority of lines of sight.

title: Peer benchmarking and digital upgrading: Field experiments on business websites
abstractText: Can low-cost comparative information trigger firms to improve the performance of a digital asset they already own? Using two large-scale randomised controlled trials with approximately 7000 UK firms in the distilling and retail sectors, we study whether peer benchmarking of website performance prompts measurable improvement. Firms receiving benchmarked website metrics and targeted recommendations exhibit modest average improvements, with more favourable effects among initially underperforming firms, consistent with partial convergence towards the industry frontier. The catch-up dynamic is strongest on mobile metrics, including as a spillover in the first experiment, in which reports contained desktop metrics only, a pattern consistent with firms focusing improvement efforts where performance gaps are greatest. Treated firms also show suggestive report-aligned increases in the adoption of mobile-optimisation and content-delivery technologies. These patterns are consistent with comparative performance information helping firms identify and respond to performance shortfalls. The findings position peer benchmarking as a scalable, low-cost instrument for narrowing the digital divide among SMEs: informational aspiration cues generate more favourable responses among firms furthest behind than among firms nearer the frontier.

title: Remote sensing and the EU nature restoration Regulation: monitoring biodiversity indicators for integrated forest management
abstractText: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear. This review synthesises current evidence on the use of RS for monitoring forest biodiversity indicators defined in the NRR and identifies methodological gaps and operational priorities. Following a systematic review of 222 studies, we evaluate the suitability of different platforms, sensors, and scales of observation. Our results show that RS capabilities are strongly indicator and scale dependent, with no single approach suitable across all indicators. Airborne laser scanning is most effective for capturing forest structural attributes, including uneven-aged forest structure, while satellite multispectral imagery provides consistent, large-scale monitoring of forest connectivity. Tree species composition and diversity can be assessed using multi-sensor approaches, though accuracy declines in mixed and structurally complex forests. In contrast, the common forest bird index cannot currently be monitored using remote sensing, and deadwood indicators are limited by the resolution required for national monitoring. Key challenges include limited availability of repeated high-resolution data, difficulties in detecting high-resolution features, and reduced classification accuracy in complex forest systems. Overall, RS has strong potential to support monitoring when integrated with National Forest Inventories and multi-sensor data streams. Advancing towards operational implementation of RS within the NRR will require harmonised products, improved methods for complex forest conditions, and greater emphasis on temporal monitoring.

title: Acrylate-Scavenging Beads Enable High-Throughput Purification of Copolymer Libraries
abstractText: Abstract High-throughput polymer science provides new opportunities to accelerate materials discovery. Acrylate copolymerization provides rapid access to diverse polymer libraries but requires equally rapid, parallel purification to remove unreacted monomers. Here, we report low-cost thiol-functionalized acrylate-scavenging beads (Beads-SH), prepared in two steps from a commercial ion-exchange resin, that efficiently remove residual acrylates through thiol-Michael addition. The beads achieved near-quantitative removal of diverse small-molecule acrylates within 12 h and remained effective in both organic solvents and water. Size-restricted access to the reactive sites within the beads minimized polymer adsorption and side reactions, with no measurable changes in polymer composition, molar mass, or dispersity. As a proof of concept, Beads-SH were used in a microplate format to purify a 72-member library of amphiphilic acrylate copolymers and evaluate polymer-mediated modulation of enzyme activity. This inexpensive, practical, and accessible strategy enables rapid purification of polyacrylate libraries for high-throughput materials discovery.

title: Spectral Criteria for Weighted Wasserstein Contractivity of Markov-Switched Iterated Function Systems
abstractText: We study one-dimensional iterated function systems in which the choice of map is governed by a finite-state Markov chain rather than by independent sampling. Let $$X\subset \mathbb R$$ be a compact interval, let $$f_1,\dots ,f_m:X\rightarrow X$$ be $$C^1$$ maps, and let $$(J_n)_{n\ge 0}$$ be a finite-state Markov chain on $$\{1,\dots ,m\}$$ with transition matrix $$P=(P_{ij})$$ . The associated random dynamical system is $$ X_{n+1}=f_{J_{n+1}}(X_n), $$ and its natural Markov state is the lifted process $$ (X_n,J_n)\in X\times \{1,\dots ,m\}. $$ We introduce the vector-valued derivative transfer operator $$ (\mathbb L\Phi )_i(x) = \sum _{j=1}^m P_{ij}|f_j'(x)|\,\phi _j(f_j(x)), \qquad \Phi =(\phi _1,\dots ,\phi _m), $$ where each component $$\varphi _i\in C(X)$$ corresponds to a switching mode. The operator acts on positive continuous vector fields on $$X$$ . Our main result proves the Collatz–Wielandt type formula $$ \rho (\mathbb L) = \inf _{\Phi >0} \max _{1\le i\le m}\sup _{x\in X} \frac{(\mathbb L\Phi )_i(x)}{\phi _i(x)}. $$ Equivalently, $$\rho (\mathbb L)$$ is the optimal contraction threshold over all continuous mode-dependent weights $$w_i:X\rightarrow (0,\infty )$$ . In particular, $$\rho (\mathbb L)<1$$ is equivalent to the existence of such weights for which the lifted Markov operator is a strict contraction along fibres with fixed mode marginal, in the associated mode-dependent weighted Wasserstein geometry. When the switching chain is irreducible and aperiodic, this fibrewise contraction combines with finite-state mode mixing to yield a unique invariant probability measure on $$X\times \{1,\dots ,m\}$$ and exponential convergence to it in a full weighted Wasserstein metric. Conversely, if $$\rho (\mathbb L)\ge 1$$ , then no continuous choice of mode-dependent weights can yield fibrewise Wasserstein contractivity of this type with contraction factor strictly smaller than one. The result gives a sharp spectral criterion for contractive geometry in Markov-switched random dynamical systems and shows explicitly how temporal correlations in the switching process affect ergodicity beyond the averaged i.i.d. theory.

title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
abstractText: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification. Mutualistic interactions are hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship remains limited. This study finds that, across Poa grasses, fungal endophytes are associated with broader niches and faster niche breadth evolution, but reduced diversification rates.

title: Campo de Dalías and the “Almeria miracle”: a cautionary tale of the value of water in agriculture
abstractText: Abstract Renowned for having one of the highest concentrations of greenhouses in the world, Campo de Dalías, located in the southeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in the southwest of the province of Almeria in Spain, offers a compelling case for understanding the evolution of how water has been valued and managed in agriculture. The region’s trajectory, from the discovery of groundwater in the 1940s, through its subsequent overexploitation, degradation, and eventual depletion, ultimately led to the adoption of water-efficient practices and the use of desalinated water for irrigation today. Here, we first investigate whether these advances in agricultural practices have increased water efficiency to levels at which water use can absorb the increased cost of sourcing it from desalination and then evaluate whether an earlier investment in these practices could have prevented the depletion of the region’s water resources. The findings demonstrate that efficiency improvements alone do not necessarily reduce total water consumption, while the lack of effective regulation of groundwater abstraction to ensure withdrawals remained below natural recharge rates meant that efficiency improvements may, at best, have delayed rather than avoided aquifer depletion. This outcome is consistent with a paradox known as the rebound effect, whereby efforts to conserve water can inadvertently enable the intensification of agricultural production, a counterintuitive consequence of efficiency improvements. The study offers valuable insights for policymakers and agricultural stakeholders facing similar challenges, highlighting the critical need for informed, integrated, and holistic participatory governance to achieve water security in an era of increasing scarcity.

title: Hydrogen-stabilized dual-phase architecture enables ductility in refractory molybdenum nanowires
abstractText: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo. Researchers report that hydrogen stabilizes a dual-phase structure in molybdenum nanowires, enabling deformation accommodation via phase transformation and dislocation nucleation. The nanowires achieve ~41.4% uniform elongation prior to fracture.

title: Encountering a newcomer attenuates shared evaluative standards: experimental evidence of rapid emergence and partial persistence
abstractText: Abstract Collective activity requires individuals to converge on common yardsticks for judging the world; however, it remains unclear how these evaluative standards (ES) respond when a group encounters unfamiliar members. Using a newly developed dot-estimation task informed by Sherif’s classic norm-formation studies, this study experimentally tracked (a) how shared ES emerge through dyadic interactions and (b) how they respond to a newcomer whose judgements systematically diverge. Participants first completed rounds with a partner whose estimates gradually aligned with their own, with perceptual bias shifting reliably toward that partner’s standard within a single block of thirty trials. However, when a newcomer with divergent estimates entered, participants partially shifted toward the newcomer’s standard, while their responses suggested carryover from the prior interaction. Impressions of the divergent newcomer did not depend on whether participants had previously established a shared standard with another partner, indicating that brief behavioural alignment does not by itself generate derogation of a divergent other. Taken together, these findings show that shared ES form quickly through dyadic interaction and, although attenuated by exposure to a newcomer, persist in part within individuals. Understanding the micro-dynamics of their formation and partial persistence helps explain how groups negotiate common standards and how those standards may attenuate—without fully unravelling—when group composition changes.

THE AUTHORIAL VOICE AND SUBJECTIVE APPROACHES IN CHOPIN'S NOVELS
abstractText: This article examines the distinctive features of authorial voice and subjective narrative approaches in the novels of the prominent American writer Kate Chopin. Particular attention is devoted to the ways in which Chopin combines narrative perspective, characterization, and genre conventions to express complex ideas concerning female identity, individual freedom, social expectations, and personal autonomy. The analysis focuses primarily on The Awakening and At Fault, considering how Chopin’s narrative choices influence the reader’s interpretation of characters and social realities. The study demonstrates that her narrative voice functions not simply as a means of presenting events but as an important artistic instrument through which conventional ideas about gender, morality, and social behavior are questioned. Chopin’s flexible treatment of literary genres also enables her to move beyond the traditional expectations of nineteenth-century American fiction.

title: IMPLEMENTASI KURIKULUM MERDEKA PADA PEMBELAJARAN SENI TARI KELAS DI IX.1 SMP ISLAM TERPADU BUDI MULIA PADANG
abstractText: This study aims to describe and analyze the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum in Dance Art learning for class IX.1 at SMP Islam Terpadu Budi Mulia Padang, focusing on the suitability of planning, implementation, and evaluation with the principles of the Merdeka Curriculum. A qualitative method with a phenomenological approach was used, with the Dance Art teacher of class IX.1 as the primary data source. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, teaching module document analysis, and documentation, then processed through data collection, data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results show that: (1) lesson planning through the teaching module generally aligns with the principles of the Merdeka Curriculum, although the Creating element of the learning outcomes was not explicitly stated; (2) implementation followed a Project Based Learning (PjBL) model across three meetings, engaging students in observing, discussing, designing, and performing a group creative dance work, although the three-meeting time allocation was not yet sufficient for the ideal PjBL stages, and some male students showed limited confidence; and (3) evaluation was carried out through diagnostic, formative, and summative assessments, with 95% of students achieving mastery on the theoretical aspect but only 65% on the practical aspect. The findings indicate that the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum in Dance Art learning has generally been consistent with its guiding principles, while time allocation and equitable student participation remain aspects that require further attention.

title: PELAKSANAAN PEMBELAJARAN SENI BUDAYA (SENI MUSIK) MENGGUNAKAN METODE DEMONSTRASI DI KELAS XI F1 SMA NEGERI 1 2 X 11 ENAM LINGKUNG
abstractText: This study aims to describe the implementation of music education using the demonstration method for the topic of musical transposition in class XI F1 at SMA Negeri 1 2×11 Enam Lingkung. Studying employs a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The research subjects were the Arts and Culture (Music) teacher and the students of class XI F1 at SMA Negeri 1 2×11 Enam Lingkung. The object of the study was the implementation of music instruction using the demonstration method for the topic of musical transposition. Data was collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, and subsequently analyzed using techniques comprising data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that the demonstration method in music instruction was implemented through preparation, execution, and evaluation stages. Supporting factors for the implementation included teacher competence, the availability of instructional media, student enthusiasm, and a conducive learning environment. Meanwhile, inhibiting factors included limited instructional time, variations in students' musical abilities, incomplete musical instruments brought by students, and a lack of focus among some students during the learning process.

title: PENGALAMAN BELAJAR SISWA PADA KEGIATAN EKSTRAKURIKULER DRUMBAND DI SMP KARTIKA 1-7 PADANG
abstractText: This study aims to describe in depth the learning experiences of students in the drumband extracurricular activities at SMP Kartika I-7 Padang. The research uses a qualitative phenomenological approach. The research instrument is the researcher themselves, assisted with observation sheets, field notes, and documentation tools. Data was collected through field observations, documentation, and in-depth interviews with the head coach, the section leader, and representatives of the instrument members. The steps to analyse the data are data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results show that students' learning experiences in drumband extracurricular activities at SMP Kartika 1-7 Padang involve active engagement, relevance, reflection, and interactivity. Active student involvement in the learning process includes activities like noting down music notation, memorising melodies, practising rhythm beats, and synchronising marching movements while playing instruments. Students find the learning relevant because the practice material has real use in supporting flag ceremonies and school events, as well as adding to their academic scores. Students reflect on themselves by evaluating technical errors during practice or performances and by changing their behaviour to be more disciplined and responsible. There is high interactivity among students through peer tutoring as an adaptive strategy to overcome the limitation of trainers, which effectively speeds up mastering music skills while instilling cooperation and care for fellow members. So, it can be concluded that students' learning experiences in the drumband extracurricular activities at SMP Kartika 1-7 Padang are meaningful through four interconnected learning experience dimensions, even when faced with various limitations, allowing them to simultaneously develop their cognitive, affective, and psychomotor aspects.

title: PENGGAMBARAN SENI VISUAL OLEH SUTRADARA PADA PEMENTASAN TEATER RAKYAT MAHASISWA SENDRATASIK FBS UNP
abstractText: This study aims to describe the role and depiction of visual arts carried out by the director in the Lenong folk theater performance titled "Beli Telor," produced by students interested in theater from the Sendratasik Education Study Program, Faculty of Language and Arts, Universitas Negeri Padang. This research uses a qualitative approach with a case study method. Data collection techniques were carried out through literature study, direct observation of the performance, in-depth interviews with the director, as well as documentation of the rehearsal and performance process. Data analysis was conducted through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. The research results show that the director plays a central role as a leader, communicator, production manager, manager of dramaturgical elements, and visual art director. In depicting visual art, the director applies a presentation concept that is simple yet effective through stage arrangement, lighting setup, makeup, costumes, use of props, and the positioning and movements of the actors (blocking). The directing style applied is a mix of a guided approach and allowing room for improvisation, so it can maintain the unique characteristics of Lenong as a communicative, humorous, and community-centered folk theater while also shaping it into a visually engaging performance. In conclusion, the director's ability to integrate all elements of a performance is the key factor in successfully realizing Lenong as a visual artwork that still preserves cultural values and the moral message intended.

title: PELAKSANAAN EKSTRAKURIKULER SENI TARI CIEK DUO TIGO DI SMP NEGERI 18 PADANG
abstractText: This study aims to describe the implementation of the Ciek Duo Tigo Dance extracurricular at SMP Negeri 18 Padang by following the steps that already exist in the extracurricular program. This activity is driven by students' interest and talent in dancing as a place to develop their potential. This type of research uses a descriptive qualitative method. The informants consist of the dance extracurricular instructor and the vice principal of student affairs at SMP Negeri 18 Padang. Data was collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, and then described through reduction, presentation, and drawing conclusions using source triangulation. The research results show that the implementation went well. Planning included program preparation, member recruitment, scheduling, as well as facilities and infrastructure. The execution took place over five meetings, namely introduction, review and memorization of movements, technique improvement, floor pattern practice, and performance simulation carried out based on aspects of wiraga, wirama, and wirasa, which showed significant improvement. This activity concluded with a performance at the farewell event for 9th-grade students and retired teachers of SMP Negeri 18 Padang on May 29, 2026. The challenges faced included limited practice space and inconsistent student attendance, but the activity still ran optimally as a platform for talent development.

title: UPAYA PELESTARIAN TARI SILEK KAIN DI SANGGAR SENI PUTI GUBALO INTAN NAGARI TALUAK KUALO KECAMATAN AIRPURA KABUPATEN PESISIR SELATAN
abstractText: This research is motivated by the importance of preserving Tari Silek Kain as one of the traditional arts that developed in Nagari Taluak Kualo, Kecamatan Airpura, Kabupaten Pesisir Selatan. The existence of this dance needs to be maintained so that it remains recognized and passed down to the younger generation. The results show that the preservation efforts for Tari Silek Kain are carried out through cultivation, development, quality improvement, and quantity increase of the dancers. Cultivation is conducted through routine practices and the transmission of dance to the younger generation. Development is achieved by adapting the dance presentation without diminishing its traditional values. Quality improvement is carried out through movement technique learning and evaluation of the dancers' abilities, while quantity increase is achieved through the recruitment of new members and the involvement of the younger generation in the studio's activities. These efforts demonstrate that Sanggar Seni Puti Gubalo Intan plays an essential role in maintaining the sustainability of Tari Silek Kain as a cultural heritage of the society in Nagari Taluak Kualo.

title: PERSEPSI PENARI TERHADAP PENGUASAAN UNSUR-UNSUR TARI PADA TARI RANTAK DI SANGGAR RANGKIANG MINANG, KECAMATAN KOTO TANGAH, KOTA PADANG
abstractText: This study aims to understand dancers' perceptions of mastering the elements of dance in the Rantak dance at Sanggar Rangkiang Minang. The dance elements studied include movement, space, time, and energy. The study uses a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. The subjects of this study are 10 dancers. Data was collected through observation, interviews, questionnaires, and documentation, then analysed by collecting, grouping, and concluding the obtained data. The results show that dancers' perceptions of mastering the elements of dance in the Rantak dance are quite good. The dancers have understood and are able to apply the elements of movement, space, time, and energy in performing the Rantak dance. Although there are still some challenges, like not maximising energy use and precise movement transitions, regular practice and guidance from the coach help the dancers improve their skills. Thus, mastering these dance elements is key to producing good Rantak dance movements that fit the dance's character.

title: SAJAK AKAR NADIR: TRANSFORMASI KETERBATASAN MENUJU KEMANDIRIAN PEREMPUAN DALAM TARI KONTEMPORER
abstractText: The creation of the contemporary dance work titled “Sajak Akar Nadir” is an artistic reflection on the struggles of women facing structural limitations, role demands, and social pressures until they successfully achieve self-sovereignty. This concept is inspired by the social reality in the film Pangku (2025) by Reza Rahardian, which was then transformed through the choreographer's personal emotional experience as an only daughter after losing her mother figure at a young age. Through the application of a dance creation method encompassing stages of exploration, improvisation, composition, and evaluation, this concept is manifested into a contemporary group dance in a dramatic-expressionist style involving 5 female dancers. Grounded in the idea that the body functions as a medium to voice unseen trauma and wounds, the visualization of this work utilizes spinning and balancing techniques rooted in the Batu Barajuik dance of West Sumatra. The work is enhanced through the symbolic integration of artistic elements such as dim lighting that creates a confined space of movement, minimal atmospheric stimulation from live techno music and vocals, as well as the use of props including threads wrapped around the head as a symbol of entanglement and stones interwoven into the hair as a symbol of perseverance in nurturing hope. The result of this dance demonstrates that the work positions women not as passive domestic objects, but as active, sovereign subjects who compose the "poem" of their own lives and attain the affirmation of independence precisely when they are at their lowest existential point (nadir).

title: SISTEM MANAJEMEN SANGGAR SENI PERMATA BUDAYA DI KOTA BATAM
abstractText: This study aims to explain and describe the Management System of Permata Budaya Art Studio in Batam City. The research uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The research instrument is the researcher themselves, aided by writing tools, a camera and a voice recorder. Data was collected through literature study, observation, interviews and documentation. The steps to analyse the data are data collection, data reduction, data presentation and drawing conclusions. The results show that the management system of Permata Budaya Art Studio consists of planning, organising, mobilising and supervision. Activity planning is done by creating short-term, medium-term and long-term programmes. Organisation is evident from a well-structured organisation, where tasks and responsibilities are clearly divided between the leader, secretary, treasurer and field coordinators. The motivational function in the Permata Budaya Art Studio is not only carried out by giving encouragement during practice but is also realised through managing performances, especially at weddings which are the studio's main activities. Mobilisation starts from the lobbying process to get a chance to perform, where the leader needs to communicate and maintain good relationships with the community, MCs, and wedding service providers. Meanwhile, supervision is carried out directly and continuously over all aspects of activities, from practice, show preparation, administration, to money management. Overall, applying this management system plays an important role in maintaining the existence of Sanggar Seni Permata Budaya and supporting efforts to preserve local dance art in Batam City.

title: ANALISIS TEKNIK PERMAINAN GITAR ELEKTRIK JOHN MAYER PADA LAGU “SLOW DANCING IN A BURNING A ROOM”
abstractText: This study aims to identify and analyse the electric guitar techniques used by John Mayer in the song "Slow Dancing in a Burning Room" from the album Continuum (2006). The research uses a descriptive qualitative method with primary data consisting of video recordings of John Mayer's performances. The results show that in the intro and interlude, bending, vibrato, and slide techniques are found, which serve to build emotional nuance and a blues character. In the verse, hybrid picking, double stop, hammer-on, and pull-off techniques are found, enriching the harmonic texture and creating expressive legato playing. Overall, these techniques are used in a structured way to form a soft, soulful musical character with a modern blues vibe, which is a trademark of John Mayer's playing.

title: PERAN DENGAR TEPI KOTA DALAM MEWADAHI PROSES KREATIVITAS MUSIK GAMAD MAHASISWA SENDRATASIK UNIVERSITAS NEGERI PADANG
abstractText: This study aims to understand the role of Dengar Tepi Kota in supporting the creative music process of Sendratasik students at Padang State University. The research uses a qualitative approach with descriptive analysis methods. The main instrument in the study is the researchers themselves, supported by tools like stationery, a mobile phone, and a camera. Data collection is done through literature review, observation, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis is carried out through stages of data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions using triangulation to test data validity. Research results show that Dengar Tepi Kota, as an output of the Gamad Music course, plays an important role as a platform for learning, creative development, and the preservation of Gamad Music for students of the Sendratasik Study Program at Universitas Negeri Padang. Its continuity from volume 1 to volume 4 shows that this activity is not only a medium to present learning outcomes but also a spark for creativity for the next generation of students to develop arrangements, performance concepts, and presentation innovations without losing the characteristics of Gamad Music. Therefore, Dengar Tepi Kota can bridge the learning process with performance practice and encourage students to keep creating creatively while still grounded in the traditional values of Gamad Music.

title: PENGGUNAAN SULUAH DALAM TARI PIRIANG SULUAH DI SANGGAR SENI AGUANG GUNUANG KOTA PADANG PANJANG
abstractText: This study aims to describe the use of suluah in the Piriang Suluah Dance at the Aguang Gunuang Art Studio in Padang Panjang City. The research focuses on the background, techniques, functions, and role of suluah in performance. The study uses a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. Data is collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, and then analysed through data reduction, data presentation, and drawing conclusions. Research results show that a torch is the main prop and a distinctive feature of the Piriang Suluah Dance, inspired by the life of the Nagari Gunuang community before the advent of electricity. Using a torch requires special techniques to keep it balanced and safe during the performance. Besides functioning as a dance prop, the torch enhances the aesthetic value, dramatic atmosphere, dancer's expression, and serves as an identity and a means of preserving the history, culture and local wisdom of the Nagari Gunuang community.
